Guidelines for realizing loans by Banks  
*64     MS. MABEL REBELLO:                        
             SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government had issued guidelines against the banks whose agents have 
allegedly been found harassing the customers for realizing the loans; 
(b) if so, the details of the protection given to the customers and the agencies 
where such complaints for redressal could be lodged; 
(c) whether such guidelines put onus on the concerned banks; and 

6    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA]                    Starred Questions  
(d) if so, what steps have been taken against the b anks in the recent cases of 
harassment as reported in the media? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) To protect the 
rights of bank customers, prevent their harassment,  etc. steps taken by Government 
of India/Reserve Bank of India (RBI), inter-alia, include the following:— 
(i) RBI has issued instructions/guidelines to banks  on 'Managing Risks and 
Code of Conduct in Outsourcing of Financial Services'. 
(ii) RBI has formulated the "Fair Practices Code for Lenders". 
(iii) RBI has issued instructions to All Commercial  Banks/NBFCs (excluding 
RRBs) regarding Credit Card Operations. 
(iv) Further, the Code of Banks' Commitments to Cus tomers formulated by 
Banking Codes and Standard Board of India (BCSBI) provides, inter-alia, 
that the collection policy of the bank be built on courtesy, fair treatment 
and persuasion and the bank follows a security repo ssession policy in 
consonance with the law. 
(v) The Indian Banks Association (IBA) has formulat ed a "Model Code for 
collection of dues and repossession of security" as  also a "Fair Practice 
Code for credit card operations" which has been recommended to banks for 
adoption and implementation. 
(b) In case of violation of the said guidelines, the cu stomers aggrieved cim lodge 
complaints with RBI's Customer Service Department, Banking Division of Department 
of Financial Services, Public Grievances Cell of concerned banks, Banking Ombudsman 
and District Consumer Forum. Further, the aggrieved can also lodge complaints with 
local police. 
(c) The guidelines issued by RBI clearly stipulate that  the banks would be 
responsible for all acts of omission or commission of their agents. RBI reserves the 
right to impose penalty on a bank for violation of guidelines under the provision of 
Banking Regulation Act, 1949. 
(d) RBI takes up the complaints with the concerned bank s and cautions them to 
ensure that such incidences do not recur in future.  In the Mid-Term Review of 
Annual Policy Statement (dated October 30,2007), RBI has observed that in view of 
the rise in the number of litigations against banks for engaging recovery agents in the 
recent past, it is felt that the adverse publicity could result in serious reputational risk 
for the banking sector as a whole. RBI has urged banks to follow prescribed specific 
considerations while engaging recovery agents and h as clarified that complaints 
received regarding abusive practices followed by a bank's recovery agent would invite 
serious supervisory disapproval. RBI would consider  imposing a temporary ban (or 
even a permanent ban in case of persistent abusive practices) for engaging recovery 
agents on those banks where strictures have been passed/penalties have been-imposed 
by a High Court/Supreme Court or against its Direct ors/Officers with regard to the 
abusive practices followed by their recovery agents.

Criteria for price-fixation of gas from KG basin  
*66.     SHRI D. RAJA: 
 SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there have been concerns voiced by certain quarters about the pricing 
of natural gas to be extracted from Krishna-Godavar i (KG) basin by Reliance 
Industries Ltd.; 
(b) if so, what is the criteria adopted in fixing the p rices of natural gas being 
extracted by Reliance from KG basin; and 
(c) what is the Government's reaction to the concerns being expressed by certain 
quarters? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MUR LI 
DEORA): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Production Sharing  Contract (PSC) provides for 
pricing of gas on the basis of sales on arms lengtkprinciples. The formula or basis on 
which the prices shall be determined for the purpos es of determining the 
Government take is required to be approved by the G overnment prior to sale of 
natural gas to the consumers/buyers. Accordingly, R IL submitted a proposal on 
18.5.07 for approval of gas price formula which was arrived at by following a bidding 
process. 
After taking into account the concerns voiced in some quarters regarding pricing of 
gas from KG Basin Block of RIL, the Government took the action of constituting an 
Empowered Group of Ministers (EGoM) to consider and  decide the issues of gas 
pricing and commercial utilization of gas under New  Exploration Licensing Policy 
(NELP). EGoM considered the price basis/formula submitted by RIL and decided the 
issue of pricing of gas under NELP.

Article 21.6.3 of the PSC for valuation of natural gas may be accepted with 
modifications.

(c) which of the States are in favour of imposing levy on commercial use of 
ground water; 
(d) whether the Prime Minister had advocated a holistic  approach to water 
conservation, instead of subsidizing it for economic and commercial use and hinted 
to "put the prices of water to save it"; and 
(e) it so, whether Government propose to launch a movem ent for water 
harvesting as a mission of conservation on a pattern adopted in Chennai? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ): (a) 
to (e) The National Congress on Ground Water was held on 11th September, 2007 at 
New Delhi. During the Congress, the discussion focu ssed on sustainable 
management of ground water. The need for strengthen ing awareness/education 
programmes and taking up of steps for enhancing wat er use efliciency was 
emphasised. The outcome of the Congress are given i n Statement (See below). The 
issue of levy on water was not discussed with the S tate Government during the 
Congress. 
The Prime Minister in his inaugural address stated that water is a national resource 
and an integrated view is to be taken of the countr y's water resources. The Prime 
Minister also emphasized the need for a paradigm sh ift in dealing with demand 
management as also on the importance of efficient, economic and more rational use 
of water. He opined that every living being has the  right to potable water. He called 
for economic use of water specially in irrigation, construction and other sectors and

Access to Finance for India's Rural Poor", has mentioned that some 66 per cent of large

farm yield and their income, emerging changes in so cial milieu and alienation of 
the individuals from family and society.

220. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have received any representation requesting removal of 
three per cent Central Sales Tax for Cotton on inter-State sale; 
(b) if so, whether Government have conceded such request of removal of Central 
Sales Tax for inter-State sale since the transport cost for those cotton is high 
comparing to overseas transportation; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and .  
(d) if not, the reason therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI S.S. 
PALANIMANICKAM): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) to (d) A consensus has been arrived at between the Government of India and 
the States to phase out Central Sales Tax (CST) on inter-State sale of goods by 
01.04.2000. As a first step, CST rate has been redu ced from 4% to 3% with effect 
from 01.04.2007. Further, it is stated that Section 8(5) of the Central Sales Tax Act, 
1956 empowers the respective State Government, if it is satisfied that it is necessary 
so to do in the public interest, to lower the tax r ate or exempt the tax-for sale in 
course of inter-State trade or commerce for any goo ds or class of goods from any 
particular place of business; or all sales of goods  or classes of goods by any dealer 
or by any class of dealers, to any person or class of persons-as may be notified by 
it.

223. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state:

and

education loans and home loans on low income and sa laried class borrowers and in 
respect of such borrowers whose children have availed education loans? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) The interest rates on adv ances are deregulated and 
banks are free to fix the rate of interest themselves with the approval of their Boards. 
Banks have been advised to fix their Benchmark Prim e Lending Rate (BPLR) after

242. SHRI N.R. GOVfNDARAJAR: Will the Minister of P ETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleasedlB state: 
(a) whether Directorate General of Hydro Carbons (DGH) have been empowered to 
oversee ever increasing exploration and production activities of private sector oil 
companies in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) to what extent the DGH have cross checked the activities of private sector oil 
companies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PAEL): (a) and (b) Government has strengthened 
Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) to exercise certain powers and functions of 
Central Government with a view to promoting sound management of the hydrocarbon 
resources in the country in respect of exploratfon and production companies including public, 
private and foreign companies having balanced regar d for environmental, safety, 
technological and economic aspects.

Paradigm shift in water policy 
276. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether scientists are concerned over the steady de cline in per capita water 
availability in the country and have called for pro per planning to reverse the 
negative trend; 
(b) whether in 1991, per capita fresh water availabilit y in the country was 2,209 
litre while it came down to only 1,820 litres in 2000 and by 2005, this is expected to 
further come down to only 1,341 litres; 
(c) whether these scientists have suggested that to ens ure availability of 
minimum fresh water to the people, there is an urge nt need for paradigm shift in 
water policy; and 
(d) whether Government have considered their suggestions? . 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) The average annual water 
availability in the country if assessed as 1869 Billion Cubic Metre (BCM) which may 
be considered to remain unchanged. The annual per c apita water availability in the 
country works out to be 2209 cubic metre as per the 1991 census. On the basis of the 
2001 census, the annual per capita water availabili ty has been estimated to 1820 
cubic metre and as per the projected population for  the year 2025, the annual per 
capita water availability is assessed as 1340 cubic metre. 
The scientists, researchers and planners have expressed concerns about the water 
resources scenario emerging due to population growt h, industrialization and 
urbanization from time to time at various fora. Sev eral research papers and 
recommendations of Seminar, Symposium, Conferences etc. have addressed these 
issues and numerous suggestions relating the need f or integrated and 
comprehensive planning for development, adoption of better management practices 
and implementation of efficient water management te chniques and water saving 
measures have been made. Observations/views have also been received in respect of 
National Water Policy (NWP) from various sources. T hese suggestions are duly 
examined and appropriately addressed. 
Measures for development and management of water re sources are undertaken 
by the respective State Governments which include c reation of storages through 
major, medium and minor irrigation projects, restoration of water bodies, rain water 
harvesting, artificial recharge to ground water ado ption of better management 
practices etc. Government of India provides necessa ry technical and fmancial 
assistance to the State Governments through various  schemes/ programmes. The 
Ministry of Water Resources encourage conservation of water including measures 
such as traditional water conservation practices, rainwater harvesting and recharge to 
ground water and adoption of better management practices.

277. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA SEKHAR: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state:

(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The M inistry of Water 
Resources (erstwhile Ministry of Irrigation) and Ce ntral Water Commission 
formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Wa ter Resources Development in 
1980. The NPP comprises of two components viz. (i) Peninsular Rivers Development 
and (ii) Himalayan Rivers Development and envisages  construction of storages on 
various river systems along with interlinking canal  systems to transfer water from 
water surplus areas to water deficit regions. Natio nal Water Development Agenpy 
(NWDA) was set up on 1982 to study the feasibility of Inter-basin water 
transfe«4>roposals and give a concrete shape to NPP . The Inter-linking propos .Is 
under NPP envisages additional benefits of 25 milli on ha. of irrigation from surface 
waters, 10 million ha. by increased use of ground w aters and generation of 34 
million KW of power apart from the incidental benef its of flood moderation, 
navigation, water supply, salinity and pollution control etc. 
Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identi fied 30 links for 
preparation of feasibility Reports (FRs). Out of th ese, FRs of 14 links under 
Peninsular Component and 2 Links (Indian portion) u nder Himalayan Component 
have already been completed. NWDA has taken up the work of preparation of 
Detailed Project Report (DPR) for one priority link  viz. Ken-Betwa under 
Peninsular Component.

consensus and cooperation of the concerned States a nd agreements with the

284. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will the Minister of WATER  RESOURCES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of M aharashtra has submitted a 
National Coastal Protection Project to get Central assistance; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that proposals from five other State Governments are still 
pending; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) by when Government propose to take decision and rel ease the Central 
assistance to the said State Governments? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (e) Scheme s for anti-sea 
erosion works are planned and implemented by the re spective State Governments. 
Ministry of Water Resources has no scheme for providing Central assistance to States 
for coastal protection. However, realizing the impo rtance of such works, Central 
Water Commission requested the State Governments to  identify the critical reaches 
and submit suitable proposal with a view to prepare  a scheme namely National 
Coastal Protection Project (NCPP) for seeking exter nal funding. Proposals from 
various States including Maharashtra have been rece ived. Government of 
Maharashtra has submitted a proposal with an estima ted cost of Rs. 195.50 crore in 
July 2002 for inclusion in the National Coastal Pro tection Project (NCPP). The 
proposal includes construction of 72.36 km. of anti  erosion works in Mumbai, 
Mumbai Suburban, Thane, Raigad, Ratnagiri and Sindu durg Districts. The 
compliances to observations of Central Water Commis sion on the proposals 
submitted by the coastal States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka and Union 
Territory(UT) of Lakshadweep for inclusion in the NCPP have not been received. UT of 
Andaman and Nicobar Islands has not submitted any proposal. 
An Approach Paper prepared by Ministry of Water Resources on NCPP had been 
forwarded by Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) t o the Asian Development 
Bank (ADB) for consideration. ADB approved administ ering technical assistance 
to the Government of India for Technical Study on " Integrated Coastal Management 
and Related Investment Development". The Project Preparation Technical Assistance 
team in its report recommended Project Preparatory Technical Assistance (PPTA) to 
prepare a project/programme in 2007 having key comp onents for (i) institutional 
strengthening, capacity building and investment sup port for coastal management; 
(ii) capacity building and investment support for c oastal protection. Based on the 
recommendation of the PPTA, an ADB Fact Funding Mis sion visited three States 
namely Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka during April-May, 2007. The Mission also 
recommended to work initially in Karnataka, Goa and  Maharashtra. Thereafter, a 
meeting was held in DEA and these three States have  been requested to confirm 
arrangement regarding mode of implementation of the project as a State sector project 
and that the fund from the ADB would be passed on t o the States on a back to back 
basis as is being done for all externally aided pro ject. The confirmation of 
Maharashtra Government has been received.

287.   SHRI BALAVANT  BAL APTE:  
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that information regarding thr ee lac square Km. water-
logged area in Sindhu region was known before the Indus Water Treaty-1960; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that India got only 9 to 10 per cent of this area; 
(c) whether there is no provision of review in the Treaty; 
(d) whether a demand for review can be made to safeguar d our national interests 
under Article 4 of the Helsinki Rules; and 
(e) if so, the details of the policy made thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) Avail able references 
indicate that water-logging in Sindhu region was known before the Indus Water Treaty 
1960. However, they do not provide any unique area of water-logging in Sindhu 
region and the area that India got. The report of t he Irrigation Commission - 1972 
states that about 10.9 lac hectares of area was aff ected in the Punjab State as 
estimated in the year 1958. Further, as per the boo k "The Indus Basin-History of 
Irrigation, Drainage and Flood Management" by CD. T hatte and Others, the 
survey in 1943 indicated that roughly an area of 0. 2 million ha. was affected by 
thur (alkali and saline soils) and sem (waterlogged) whereas the aerial 
reconnaissance survey got conducted by Government o f Pakistan in 1954 indicated 
that an area of more than 4.45 million ha. in West Pakistan was poorly drained and 
water-logged. 
(c) Relevant provisions of the Treaty (Article XII Final Provisions) which provide 
for its review are given below:— 
"(3)   The provisions of this Treaty may from time to time be modified by a duly 
ratified treat concluded for that purpose between the two Governments.  
(4) The provisions of this Treaty, or the provision s of this Treaty as modified 
under the provisions of Paragraph (3), shall contin ue in force until 
terminated by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the 
two Governments".  
(d) The Helsinki Rules governing use of International W atercourses 1966 are 
guidelines adopted by the International Law Associa tion (ILA), a private body of 
lawyers are not binding upon States. 
(e) Does not arise.

Cooperation of Bangladesh in the investigation into Hyderabad twin blasts  
*81.    SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:†† 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that 2-day Home Secretary level talks between India and 
Bangladesh

2    Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA]                    to Questions  
held in the month of August, 2007 agreed to take sw ift action on actionable 
intelligence on insurgents and fugitives to be shar ed between law enforcement 
agencies of the two countries; 
(b) if so, whether Government has sought the cooperatio n of Bangladesh in the 
investigation on the 25th August Hyderabad twin blasts wherein Bangladeshis have 
been held responsible; 
(c) whether those held responsible have been handed over to India; and 
(d) the steps, Bangladesh has taken to check the infiltration of Bangladeshis into this 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL): (a) to (d) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) In the Home Secretary level talks between India and Bangladesh held in New 
Delhi on 2nd-3rd August, 2007, both sides, interalia, agreed to initiate swift action 
on information received about groups and elements a nd other fugitives from the 
law of either country taking shelter in the other country. 
(b) and (c) The case of twin blast at Hyderabad on 25-0 8-2007 is still under 
investigation by the State Police. 
(d) The issue of illegal infiltration from Bangladesh into the country has been taken 
up by the Government with the Government of Banglad esh at various fora. The 
Government has no inputs about the steps taken by t he Government of Bangladesh 
to check the infiltration of Bangladeshis into the country. 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Sir, the hon. Minister has given the reply but I am not 
satisfied with that. What action has the Government  taken during the year 2007 to 
pursue with the Government of Bangladesh of the clo sure of training camps in its 
territory which have been imparting training to ins urgents and jihadis and what has 
been the result of such an interaction in the reduc tion of the number of militants' 
camps in the last ten months? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, we are dealing with a foreign country and we have a 
mechanism for discussing such issues with Bangladesh. The issues are discussed at 
three levels. One level is that of the DGs, the Director Generals of Police; the second 
level is that of the Joint Secretaries and the third level is that of the Secretary in the 
Home Department here and the Interior Ministry over  there. They have been 
discussing these issues. But the reply we get from them is that there are no insurgents 
or terrorists having their camps over there and that if those facts are brought to their 
notice, they will take action. We have been exchang ing information between the 
Governments, giving information about the camps and  yet, unfortunately, it has 
not been possible to see that some effective action  is taken. What we get is the 
denial. We are in the process of discussing these m atters at higher levels also. At 
the Home Ministers' level this matter has been disc ussed; at the External Affairs 
Ministers' level, this matter has been discussed; at the Prime Minister's level also,

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, the Home Minister s aid in his reply 
that at the Home Secretary level talks between Indi a and Bangladesh both sides 
agreed to initiate swift action on information rece ived about militant groups. So, I 
would like to ask the Minister, Sir, whether it is true that the investigators have come 
across links between the blasts in Hyderabad this y ear and the organisations in 
Bangladesh and had sought the assistance of their counterparts in tracking down the 
origin of the phone calls in the neighbouring count ry; also, whether it is true that 
the Home Ministry had received information from sec urity agencies about the 
detention of Mohammad Hamza, a key functionary of H UJI and prime suspect in 
the blast case and whether response has been receiv ed from Bangladesh to the 
Interpol notice for Hamza. 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, we have been discussing  this matter with 
Bangladesh. As far as Interpol notice is concerned,  there is an international 
agreement and we follow that international agreemen t and it is expected that the 
States, the Governments of the different countries do help them. We are in the 
process of investigating into the matters relating to the incidents in Hyderabad. It 
will be premature, at this stage, to disclose the information because disclosure of the 
information, at mis stage, will affect the case. We  do have some clues and we are 
following those clues. We have given the informatio n relating to those to our 
neighbouring States and we hope that we will get the assistance and cooperation.

Joint strategy for countering threats from various militant groups 
*82 SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of  HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a 3-day annual conference  of Director-Generals and 
Inspector-Generals of Police, organized by the Inte lligence Bureau was held in the 
month of October, 2007 to discuss a joint strategy with police chiefs from all States, 
para-military forces and security agencies on countering threats from various militant 
groups;  
(b) whether top officials have sought a policy for close monitoring of procedures for 
providing security to various persons; 
(c) if so, the outcome of the conference held; and 
(d) the concrete steps being taken to meet the threat of terrorists in various 
States? 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL): (a) to (d) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) Yes, Sir. The Annual Conference of Directors Genera l of Police/Inspectors 
General of Police of States/UTs and Heads of Central Police Organizations was held 
from October 3 to 5, 2007 in New Delhi. 
(b) The issue of VVIP Security was also discussed in the Conference. 
(c) This Conference is held every year to deliberate on  new challenge, exchange 
ideas on best practices and formulate strategies an d measures to strengthen various 
aspects of management of internal security. 
(d) The Government reamins fully committed to combating  the menace of 
terrorism. The policy of the Government is to count er the challenge posed by 
terrorism by way of a multi-pronged strategy. In pu rsuance of this strategy, the 
Government has taken various measures on political, legal, security and development 
fronts. The Government is willing to talk to all th ose groups who agree to abjure 
violence and surrender arms within the framework of  the Indian Constitution. The 
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 as amended in September, 2004 has the 
necessary provision to deal with various aspects of  terrorism. On the security front, 
the counter terrorism measures include effective bo rder management to check 
infiltration across the borders, deployment of Cent ral Forces to aid the State Police 
Forces in areas prone to terrorist violence, height ened vigil and security 
arrangements in vulnerable areas and around vital i nstallations, strengthening of 
intelligence gathering and sharing capabilities, particularly at the cutting edge level, 
augmentation and modernization of police forces and  raising of India Reserve 
Battalions ensuring improved technology, weaponry and equipment with the Central 
and State Police Forces and steps taken to achieve bilateral and multi-lateral 
cooperation to deal with the global imperatives of terrorism. 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, some of the hon. Member s had expressed some 
apprehensions about investigations and all those things. That is also being looked into. 
When it is taken up, we will discuss it. The Govern ment is willing to participate in 
the discussion at any time, in accordance with your directions.

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, one of the greatest  challenges facing 
the country today is the threat from Maoist violence, which has taken over 400 lives. It 
is almost three times more than those lost in Jammu and Kashmir. But, Sir, there does 
not seem to be a comprehensive strategy against thi s Left-wing extremism. Andhra 
Pradesh has its own strategy; Chhattisgarh has its own strategy, and so on and so 
forth. 
Sir, since the problem cuts across State boundaries, and the States would need to 
pursue a coordinated approach to meet this challenge, has the Government established 
a functional inter-State mechanism under the Intell igence Bureau or any other 
agency to tackle the threat of terrorism in a more concerted manner? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, this is a very good question. Sir, we have the central 
agencies collecting the information. And the information collected by the agencies is 
shared with the State Governments. This is one steps we are taking. 
The second step which we have taken is this. For th e information of this august 
House, I would like to say that 33 battalions of pa ramilitary forces are given to the 
States which are affected by the naxalite movement.  There are 33 battalions. It is 
nearly equal to 30.000 men and officers. 
Then, we have asked the State Governments to have a  unified command. That is, 
we are not in a position to deploy the forces which are given to the State Governments. 
So, when the forces are given to the State Governme nts, they shall have to deploy 
the State Police as well as the union police in a manner they like. The liberty is given 
to them, and it is expected that the Chief Minister of the State would head the unified 
command and give directions to them. 
The third thing which we have done is that we have identified the districts which are 
affected by the naxalite movement. And, we are not only trying to deal with the police 
forces, or with the gun and the bullet, but are giv ing extra funds to the State 
Governments to develop those districts. Funds are g iven over and above what is 
already given to them. Not only that, we have given  them the UAV in Chhattisgarh 
which is the worst affected State. And allow me to say this that I do not want to take 
any political stand as such. Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand are the two States because of 
which more than 50 per cent of incidents and deaths are taking place. It is only because 
of these two States. And, these two States are the States which are contributing to the 
naxalite activities. When the naxalite activity in Andhra Pradesh has come down by 60 
per cent, the naxalite activity in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand has gone up by more 40 
per cent and 50 per cent. Incidents and deaths are taking place. We are helping them 
also. ...(Interruptions)...  
DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: Does it mean that the naxa lites have been 
exported to Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand? ...(Interruptions)...  
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Let me complete ...(Interruptions)... I will reply to your 
question. ...(Interruptions)... I will reply to our question. ..(Interruptions).. I am 
giving the facts. ..(Interruptions)... I am giving the facts. ...(Interruptions)... I am not 
blaming any Government. ..(Interruptions).. I am giving the facts. ..(Interruptions).. 
The fact is this. Now, this has to be understood. M oreover, we have asked the State 
Governments to recruit more persons in their police. Some of the State Governments 
are having 10,000 vacancies in the police. If you h ave 10,000 vacancies in police 
force, which has 50,000 men, how can you manage these thing? And, we are expected 
to manage from here. Suppose, we try to manage from  here, naturally, the objection 
will be raised by you only saying that constitutionally we cannot do anything. We are 
living in a federal system. The Constitutional arra ngement does not allow it. But,

interfere in one State, naturally, you would expect us to

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, actionable intellig ence is the only 
way to foil any threats from the terrorist groups w ho are using modern technology 
and very sophisticated weapons. My question is: Whe ther the Ministry of Home 
Affairs has drawn up a plan for modernisation of ga dgets and technologies that are 
used for intelligence gathering. Though I know you have Constitutional handicaps 
and restrictions, I would like to know whether the States have been asked to draw up 
similar plans. Though the Central has allocated a l ot of funds for the States, in the 
past, the Home Minister had said that the States ha ve not fully utilised those funds. 
So, what plans do you have and how do you propose t o ensure that the States 
upgrade their gadgets and technologies, because, ot herwise, the war on terrorism 
cannot be fought effectively? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: This is exactly what we have done, Sir. Now, we are 
strengthening the intelligence agencies at the national level — the defence intelligence — 
RAW, IB and all those things. That information is collected. Then, collectively, that 
information is scanned. Thereafter, the relevant in formation is passed on. For this 
purpose, modernisation scheme is drawn up, and that  scheme is being implemented. 
But, this is not enough. It is necessary for the St ate Intelligence Departments to 
strengthen themselves. That is why, we have prepared, some suggestions and given 
to them, as to what kind of equipment they should p rocure, what kind of training 
they should give, how many people they should have in the special branches, and if 
the officers are not ready to work in the special branches, what special facilities should 
be given to them and all those things. So, information has been given to them. I .am 
happy to inform the House that some States have realised that if Naxalite activity or 
terrorist activity, or any violent activity is to be controlled, then, more than the gun, 
the intelligence is important. They should rely upo n intelligence. They are 
strengthening their intelligence agencies. For inst ance, Andhra Pradesh is doing, 
Maharashtra is doing, Karnataka is doing, Tamil Nadu is also doing something and 
some other States are also doing it. But the movement in this direction, started by the 
State Government, is a little slower. We are giving a lot of funds to them. We are asking 
them to have a holistic plan, so that, not only the intelligence and training but also the 
back up of the action, which has to be taken, shoul d be considered. We have asked 
them to prepare the plans themselves in consultation with the Union Government as to 
how the plan should be refined, also in consultatio n with the adjoining State 
Government and do it. So, we are also helping them in every respect, but direct action 
is not permitted by the constitution. Excepting direct action, any other help which is

Committee for upgradation of ITIs 
*84.    SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:   
SHRI MAHMOOD A. MADANI: 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleas ed to state: 
(a) whether Government has constituted any Committee fo r the upgradation of 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs); 
(b) if so, the composition and the mandate of such Committee; and 
(c) what is the level of participation of private sector in this Committee? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND  
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) to (c) Gover nment of India 
took up upgradation of 500 Government ITIs in the c ountry on the basis of budget 
speech of Union Finance Minister, 2004-05 as follows: 
(a) Upgradation of 100 ITIs through domestic funding at a cost of Rs. 160 
crore since 2005-06. 
(b) Upgradation of 400 ITIs through World Bank assistance at a cost of Rs. 1581 
crores since 2006-07. 
Union Finance Minister announced upgradation of the  remaining 1396 
Government ITIs by providing an interest free loan of upto Rs. 2.5 crore per ITI in 
Public Private Partnership mode in his budget speech of 2007-08. 
Under these Schemes, an Institute Management Commit tee (IMC) is being 
constituted in each ITI to accomplish the task of upgradation. IMCs are being headed 
by an Industry Partner. There are four other members from the Industry on the I.M.C. 
The remaining five members are from the Government and Principal of the ITI is 
the member secretary of the IMC. 
The IMC has mandate for upgradation of training infrastructure in the ITI in such a 
way that the quality of training is good and demand  responsive. The participation 
from the industry has been very enthusiastic so far. Though financial contribution is not 
a pre-condition for participation, many industry partners have come forward by way 
of equipment, tools, machinery as well as financial resources. 
Under Scheme (b) and the Scheme "Upgradation of 1396 Govt. ITIs through PPP" 
National Steering Committees at Central level and S tate Steering Committees at 
State levels have also been constituted. Compositio n and functions of these 
committees are attached as Statement-I and II.

Import of Chinese toys  
†*85. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of COMME RCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons of returning to China the toys imported by America in the year 2007; 
(b) whether it is a fact that China is supplying those toys to India which were returned 
by America; 
(c) whether there exists a system to check the quality of toys imported from China; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI KAMAL NATH): 
(a) to (e) There is no firm information available with Government of India about return of 
imported toys by America to China in the year 2007. Similarly there is no information 
available regarding China supplying the toys to India, which were returned by America. 
However, it is understood that in recent months, the largest number of recalls of toys 
imported from China into USA has been due to United States Consumer Product Safety 
Commission having found excess level of lead paint, violating the US Government lead 
paint standard. There were some other toys/ children articles which were recalled due to 
design or manufacturing defects which had or could have caused injury. Among the most 
extensive recalls of this nature was the recall of Barbie and Tanner magnetic toys by 
MATTEL due to magnets coming loose which could be swallowed by children. There 
were also cases of toys recalled due to fire/burning hazard.

Toys are classified under Chapter 95 of ITC (HS) Cl assification of Export and 
Import items. Import of toys is free. As per Foreig n Trade Policy, all imports are 
subject to domestic laws, rules, orders, regulation s, technical specifications, 
environmental and safety norms as applicable to domestically produced goods. 
As regards the safety requirement for toys, the Bur eau of Indian Standards has 
published the following three standards for safety requirement for toys:— 
1. IS 9873 (Part-I): 2001/ISO 8124-1:2000 Safety requi rements for toys: Part 
1: Safety aspects related to mechanical and physical properties. 
2. IS 9873 (Part 2): 1999/ISO 8124-2:1994 Safety requi rements for toys: Part 
2: Flammability requirements. 
3. IS 9873 (Part 3) 1999/ISO 8124-3:1997 Safety requirements for toys; Part 3: 
Migration of certain elements, perscribed maximum a cceptable element 
migration, for Antimony (Sb), Arsenic (As), Barium (Ba), Cadmium (Cd), 
Chromium (Cr), Lead (Pb), Mercury (Hg) and Selenium  (Se) from toy 
materials. 
The aforementioned BIS standards are neither mandat ory on domestic 
manufacturers nor on imports. Ministry of Micro, Me dium and Small Enterprises

Eradication of child labour  
*91. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of policy initiative measures that have been taken or proposed to be taken 
by Government to eradicate child labour in the country; 
(b) the details of efforts made so far by Government in this respect; and 
(c) the details of schemes formulated and being impleme nted by Government 
alongwith the funds allocated for the purpose in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND  
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) to (c) The National Policy-on Child 
labour envisages strict enforcement of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 
1986 with simultaneous efforts towards rehabilitation of both parents and children through 
a project based action plan linkages with the poverty eradication and income generation 
programmes of the Government. Considering the magnitude and nature of the problem, 
Government is following a gradual and sequential approach of initially covering children 
working in hazardous occupations and process. Under the Child Labour (Prohibition & 
Regulation) Act, 1986 there are 15 occupations and 57th process banned for the 
employment of children below the age of 14 years. State Governments are the appropriate 
authority for the enforcement of the Act for the arexs under their jurisdiction. 
For the rehabilitation of child labour Government is implementing the National Child 
Labour Project (NCLP) Scheme in 250 districts of the country. Under the Scheme, children 
withdrawn from work are admitted into special schools, where they are provided with 
education, vocational training, mid-day meal, stipend and health care facilities etc. In 
addition, INDUS Child Labour Project, a jointly funded Project of Government of India 
and US Department of Labour is also being implemented in 21 districts. Government is 
also implementing a Scheme of Grants-in-aid to Voluntary Organization in the districts, 
which are not covered under NCLP/INDUS Projects. An amount of Rs. 175 crores has been 
allocated for the purpose under these schemes during the current financial year.

The Ministry of Labour and Employment is regularly monitoring the implementation of 
these schemes through periodical reports, visits, inspections and review meetings. The Central 
Monitoring Committee on Child Labour headed by Union Labour Secretary, with Labour 
Secretaries of all States implementing the child labour schemes as members, reviews in detail 
the implementation of these schemes by the State Governments and suggests corrective action 
wherever necessary. 
For the 11th Plan, the Ministry has proposed expansion of the NCLP Scheme to 600 
districts of the country. In addition, certain other additional features in the Scheme have also 
been proposed, viz. residential schools for migrant children in big cities, vocational training for 
adolescents in the age group of 14 to 17 years, greater State level monitoring and awareness 
generation. 
Last year, Government took a major step towards the elimination of child labour by banning 
the employment of children as domestic servants and in dhabas, hotels, roadside eateries. A 
large number of children all over the country are working in these two occupations. 
The Ministry is taking various measures to cover the families of child labour under the 
developmental schemes of other Ministries to help in their economic upliftment so that 
they are not compelled to send their children to work. A Core Group on Convergence has 
also been formed under the Chairpersonship of Union Labour Secretary involving other 
Ministries concerned viz. Human Resource Development, Women & Child Development, 
Rural Development, Urban Housing and Poverty Alleviation, Social Justice & Empowerment, 
Health etc., so that these families can get the benefit of the Schemes of these ministries also. 
The ministry is also regulairly conducting awareness generation campaigns on the issue. 
Recently, beginning from 14th  November, 2007, the Ministry has launched a fortnight long 
drive to step up enforcement of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act. The 
State Governments have been requested at the level of Chief Ministers to bake all necessary 
measures for ensuring legal compliance and creation of mass awareness against the evil of 
child labour. Funds have also been allocated to them specially for carrying out awareness 
generation campaign during the period.

*99. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of R URAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has reviewed the progress of the  implementation of the 
National Rural Employment Guarantee programme; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the names of States which are lagging behind in the  implementation of 
National Rural Employment Guarantee programme; and 
(d) the steps taken by Government against these States? 

Written Answers to [21 NOV. 2007]   Starred Questions     37 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (DR. RAGHUVANSH 
PRASAD SINGH): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Review of the progress of the implementation 
of NREGA is done on regular basis NREGA has been re viewed at the highest level 
in Prime Minister's review meeting on 20.6.2007. Pe rformance Review Committee 
meetings are undertaken by the Minister of Rural Development and Secretary (Rural 
Development) from time to time. During the year 200 7-08, three Regional Review 
Committee meetings have been held to cover review o f all States. These were held 
at Orissa, Guwahati and Jaipur. A Central Employmen t Guarantee Council was 
constituted on 22.9.2006 to review and monitor the implementation of the Act. The 
Council has so far held three meetings and reviewed  the implementation of 
NREGA. Members of the Council also conduct field visits in various States to oversee 
the progress of the Act. An Executive Committee con stituted under the Central 
Council reviewed the progress of the Act in its meeting held on 16.8.2007. 
Progress of NREGA was also shared in the interactiv e session with Members of 
Parliament held during 20th - 23rd August, 2007 and  5th -6th September, 2007. 
National Level Monitors (NLMs) and Area Officers of  the Ministry visit various 
districts to oversee the progress of the Act. the A rea Officers have been directed to 
cover 10 village during their each visit. Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have 
also been set up to review the implementation of the Act. 
(c) and (d) NREGA is demand driven. The pace of imp lementation of the Act 
varies from State to State based on the scale and v olume of demand in a particular 
context. During the year 2006-2007, a total of 2.12 crore households had demanded 
employment, out of which, 2.10 crore were provided employment. During the current 
year upto September, 2007 a total of 1.98 crore hou seholds have demanded 
employment, out of which, 1.88 crore have been provided employment. However, in 
some States the implementation of the Act has been affected due to State Assembly 
elections and also due to natural calamities like r ains, floods etc. As employment is 
provided under the Act on demand, there are not fixed targets and therefore  it is not 
correct to say that a particular State is lagging behind.

principle' approval to the recommendations of the Committee in September 2003. 
The Committee identified two interrelated issues viz., high age profile and career 
stagnation. The Committee made a total of 15 recomm endations encompassing

peel factors, which include a strategy to bring dow n the age profile through a 
lasting solution and also short-term measures to provide some immediate relief. 
Certain recommendations pertaining to non-select ra nks have already been 
implemented with effect from December 2004. Review of the creation of posts and 
restructuring of the cadres in the forces is an ongoing and continuous process.

Commission (NHRC) has registered 1,21,313 number of complaints of human rights 
violations, which includes cases brought forward from previous year as well as fresh 
institution during the current year (2006-07). Duri ng the period from 1st April, 
2006 to 31st March, 2007, the Commission disposed o ff 93,421 cases (77% 
disposal).

Andhra Pradesh from 1.4.2007 to 12.11.2007 and disp osed off 4005 cases during 
this period (which includes cases carried forward from the previous years).

eighteen States, including State of Andhra Pradesh, have set up State Human Rights

accountability of public servant Since its establishment in October, 1993 the NHRC has 
been recommending interim relief to the victims of the next of  kin of deceased victims in 
appropriate cases.

†335. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that terrorism is becoming a c hallenge for Government 
inside the country and on the borders in the country; 
(b) if so, whether Government is contemplating stringent steps to wipe it out; 
and

not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAI RS (SHRI 
SHRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (a) to (c) The Govt. is aware of the challenge posed by 
terrorism, which has now become a global phenomenon . The Government remains 
fully committed to combating the menance of terrori sm by way of a multi-pronged 
strategy. In pursuance of this strategy, the Government has taken various measures on 
political, legal, security and development fronts. The Government is willing to talk to 
all those groups who agree to abjure violence and s urrender arms within the 
framework of the Indian Constitution. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 
1967 as amended in September, 2004 has the necessar y provisions to deal with 
various aspects of terrorism. On the security front , the counter terrorism measures 
include effective border management to check infilt ration across the borders, 
deployment of Central Forces to aid the State Polic e Forces in areas prone to 
terrorist violence, heightened vigil and security a rrangements in vulnerable areas and 
aound vital installations, strengthening of intelli gence gathering and sharing 
capabilities, particularly at the cutting edge leve l, augmentation and modernization 
of police forces and raising of India Reserve Batta lions, ensuring improved 
technology, weaponry and equipment with the Central  and State Police Forces, and 
steps taken to achieve bilateral and multi-lateral cooperation to deal with the global 
imperatives of terrorism. Rise in suicide cases in the country

341. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HOME  AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that incidents of kidnapping f or ransom and killing have 
increased during the last two years; 
(b) if so, the details of cases during the last five years; 
(c) in how many cases the police could rescue the victim and arrest the culprits and 
cases where it failed; and 
(d) what special steps are proposed to be taken to prevent kidnapping of innocent 
people? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAI RS (SHRI 
MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) As per information obtained from the State Governments/ 
Union Territory Administration and compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau

trend. NCRB does not maintain data on kidnapping for killings. 
(b) The State/UT-wise details of cases registered under kidnapping and abduction for 
ransom during 2002 to 2006 have been indicated at Statement-I (See below) 
(c) State/UT-wise details of cases registered, cases chargesheeted, cases convicted, 
persons arrested, persons chargesheeted and persons convicted under kidnapping and 
abduction during 2002 to 2006 have been indicated at Statement-II (See below) 
(d) 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State subejcts under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India and therefore, the State Governments are primarily responsible 
for prevention, detection, registration and investi gation of crime including 
kidnapping of innocent people and for prosecuting t he criminals through the 
machinery of their law enforcement agencies. The Mi nistry of Home Affairs, 
however, supplements the efforts of the State Gover nments by providing them 
financial assistance for modemization  of their Police Forces in terms of weaponry, 
communication, equipment, mobility, training and ot her infrastructure under the 
Scheme of Modernization of State Police Forces. Fur ther, intelligence inputs are 
regularly shared by the Central Security and Intelligence Agencies with the State Law 
Enforcement Agencies to prevent crime and law and order related incidents. The State 
Governments are also advised from time to time to g ive more focused attention to 
improving the administration of criminal justice sy stem and take such measures as 
are necessary for the prevention of crimes.

371. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether with economy registering a regular growth o f 7 to 9 percent every 
year, unemployment has out-stripped all economic growth; 
(b) if so, the comparative figures of economic growth, growth in employment and 
unemployment over the last three years, indicating the number of the unemployment 
generated both in rural and urban sector during these years; and 
(c) the main reasons for increase in unemployment and t he concrete steps 
proposed to be taken to deal with this menace? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND  
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) and (b) Reli able estimates of 
employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial labour force survey 
conducted by National Sampled Survey Organisation a nd estimates of Gross 
Domestic Product (GDP) are obtained through Nationa l Accounts Statistics 
compiled by Central Statistical Organisation. As pe r these reports, the Indian 
Economy registered an average annual growth rate of 6.7% during 1993-94 to 1999-
2000 and 5.98% during 1999-2000 to 2004-2005, whereas the annual rates of growth 
of employment as on usual status basis during these  periods were 0.98% and 2.95% 
as against unemployment growth rate of 3.23% and 3. 7%. Number of unemployed 
persons was estimated to have increased from 9.04 m illion in 1999-2000 to 10.84 
million in 2004-05, resulting into an increase of 1 .80 million (1.15 million in rural 
and 0.65 million in urban areas). 
(c) Increase in unemployment is mainly attributed t o higher rate of growth of 
working age population than total population, incre ase in labour force participation 
rates, particularly among women and higher unemploy ment among educated youth. 
Approach paper to 11th Five Year Plan envisages cre ation of 70 million job 
opportunities during the Plan period and in order t o achieve this target, rate of 
growth of non agricultural employment is to be accelerated to 5.8% per annum from 
4.7% in 1999-2005.

(c) NREGA is demand driven and not an allocation based programme. A National 
Employment Guarantee Fund has been established for providing funds to the States for 
implementation of the Act. Provisions are made in the budget for implementation of the 
Act on the basis of funds utilized by the States and also on the basis of demand for work

crore had been released by the Centre to the various states. NREGA is demand driven.

to an over all ceiling of 100 days of employment in  a financial year per household. 
Therefore, no targets can be fixed for providing employment under the Act.

Present status of PMGSY  
389. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the Minister of RURAL  
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) what are the reasons for Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) 
lagging behind the planned completion targets; 
(b) the action taken to complete PMGSY as per schedule; and 
(c) the present status of PMGSY, State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU): (a) to (c) A statement 
indicating physical and financial progress in implementation of Pradhan Mantri Gram 
Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is enclosed. (see below) "Rural Roads" being a State subject, 
Projects under PMGSY are executed by State/UT Governments through their agencies 
i.e. SRRDA (State Rural Roads Development Agency) for mo nitoring, financial 
management and coordination at the State Level and Programme Implementation 
Units (PIUs) for programme implementation at the district level. In the case of Bihar 
and Tripura, Central Agencies have also been entrus ted with the implementation of 
PMGSY. Some of the major constraints affecting the pace of implementation of the 
programme are:— 
• Constraint of non-availability of adequate technical manpower. 
• Procedural delay in tendering and award of works. 
• Inadequate capacity of the Programme Implementation Units. 
• Adverse climatic conditions. 
• Non availability of critical construction material. 
Steps have been taken for stepping up the pace of i mplementation of the 
programme through enhanced allocation of funds, aug mentation of contracting 
capacity through modifications in Standard Bidding Document, provision of interest 
free advance to the contractors for procurement of plant and machinery, training of 
field staff including contractor's personnel, continuous and regular monitoring of the 
programme. States have also been advised to increas e the number of programme 
implementing units, wherever necessary to ensure timely completion of the process of 
tendering and award of projects and also to strengt hen contract management for 
ensuring timely execution of projects.

Scheme for unemployed textile workers due to rupee appreciation  
414. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to frame a scheme, especiall y for textile workers, who 
lost their jobs due to slump inexports due to appreciation in rupee; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES ( SHRI 
E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN): (a) to (c) While there has bee n an impact on exports of 
textiles goods on account of the appreciation of th e rupee as compared to the US 
dollar, this impact has been mainly felt in the pri vately owned garmenting sector. 
Some measures have been introduced to offset this i mpact. These measures, inter-
alia, include (i) Increase in Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) rates by 3% for 
textiles (including handloom), readymade garments, handicrafts; (ii) Increase in duty 
drawback rates across product categories; and (iii)  Reduction in pre and post 
shipment credit by 2%, and ECGC cover premium by 10 per cent. It is expected that 
the exporting units will take advantage of these incentives.

Bum La in Tawang District of Arunachal Pradesh. I would like to know whether the 
Government of India is aware of this happening or not.

two countries. Recently, it has come out in the print media that the Chinese Advisor, 
attached to the Chinese foreign ministry has openly claimed that Tawang belongs to

to China whereas the total area of Arunachal Pradesh is nearly 84,000 sq. kms.

territory. We feel a lot of insecurity there and we  are not able to know as to what 
stand the Government of India is taking. We are tol d that a lot of negotiations are

Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India, and, therefore, please do not keep us in 
the hanging position. We really want to know what e xactly is the Government of 
India doing.

placed it somewhere down below Tawang. Why has this act of cowardice been done

statement on the stand taken by the Government of India on

ORAL ANSWERS TO  QUESTIONS  
*101. [The questioner (Shri Raj Nath Singh) was absent. For answer vide pages 
18-19 infra. ]  
Conservation of Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge 
*102. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:†† 
SHRI HARISH RAWAT. 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the elements of the National Programme for Prom oting Conservation of 
Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge; 
(b) the organizational structure set up to implemen t various objectives of the 
programme and hat manner the finances are being del egated to the participating 
States; and 
(c) the number of States which have identified the sites for the conservation of 
medicinal the details of the medicinal plants. State-wise, and area-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) A project entitled "National Programme on Promo ting Conservation of 
Medicinal Plants and Traditional Knowledge for Enha ncing Health and Livelihood 
Security" has been taken up in  he States, namely K erala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, 
Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Man arashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh, with financial support from United Nations  Development Programme 
(UNDP). The project started in May, 2006 with UNDP contribution of US $ 3 
million (approx. Rs. 12 crores), to be completed in  four and half years. The main 
elements of the project include: establishment of a system for rapid threat assessment 
and trade regulation; a network of Medicinal Plant Conservation Areas (MPCAs), 
State level medicinal plant seed centre; method for  sustainable harvest and 
augmentation; home herbal garden; coummunity knowle dge registers and 
mainstreaming traditional medicine into official primary helth programme. 
The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Santosh Bagrodia . 

2    Oral  Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
(b) The Union Ministry of Environment and Forests is th e National Executing 
Agency for the programme and the Foundation for Rev italization of Local Health 
Tradition (FRLHT), Bangalore is the technical coord inating agency. The Forest 
Departments of the concerned States are the designa ted nodal agencies for 
implementation. The funds are released by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to 
the FRLHT for further release to the implementing agencies. The funds so disbursed 
are reimbursed by UNDP to the Government. 
(c) Under the project only four States viz. Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, West Bengal 
and Rajasthan were required to identify sites for c onservation. Of these, three States 
namely Madhya Pradesh, Orissa and Rajasthan have identified sites for conservation 
upto October, 2007. Teams of Taxonomists have been constituted for inventorisation 
of medicinal plants. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, medicinal plants are very important not only 
for our country but for humanity, as a whole, becau se the kind medicines that are 
produced from them are good even for life threatening diseases. Some very important 
medicines which are made out of them are very impor tant. For example, 
cyclosphorine is used in every transplant case. Wha t I am trying to say is that we 
must try to save them. We must identify them and save them. But the management of 
these particular plants in the Government is handled by many Ministries. I would like 
to know which are the different Ministries who are handling this job because what is 
happening is that these plants are exported to Chin a at a very low rate and, then, in 
China they are re-exporting these at a much higher rate. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: What is the question? 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: What is the Government plann ing so that this 
situation can be reversed? In fact, we should be ab le to process our plants in our 
own country. 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, in the Ministry of Env ironment and 
Forests we are doing the conservation of the medici nal plants. The hon. Member 
wants to know how many Departments or Ministries ar e doing the job for medicinal 
plants. Sir, I would like to inform the hon. Member, through you, that in Government 
of India there is a National Medicinal Plant Board under the Department of AYUSH 
in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. That is the nodal agency for the 
conservation, development, processing and marketing of the medicina. plants. So far as 
research work is concerned, the Ministry of Science and Technology is involved in the 
research and promotion. The DBT, DHT and CSIR are doing this job. In the Ministry 
of Agriculture there are institutions like ICAR, Na tional Horticulture Mission, 
National Board for Horticulture, etc. which are doing cultivation and breeding aspects 
of the medicinal plants. The Ministry of Commerce is involved in the marketing and 
export of the medicinal plants whereas my Ministry,  the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests, is doing conservation and protection a nd also some promotional job 
through some special projects. So far as the questi on that some plants are being 
exported to China and other countries is concerned,  Sir, I would like to inform the 
hon. Member that there is an Act known as Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and under 
that if any flora or fauna is to be sent outside, p ermission will have to be obtained 
from the authority concerned. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, my second supplementary  is that the 
Ministry has identified under the project only four  States to identify sites for 
conservation. Rajasthan is one of them. They have already identified. I would like to 
know from the hon. Minister what kind of financial, assistance is offered to the State 
for the development of plant and also what is happe ning to the home herbal garden 
schemes amongst various citizen towns because these  plants do not require large 
spaces and this is like dadi's medicine, Sir, if these plants can be developed at home, 
then, a lot of medical problems can be solved at home only. 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions   3 
SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA: Sir, we are running a progr amme that is 
called National Programme on Promoting Conservation  of Medicinal Plants in 
traditional knowledge for enhancing health and live lihood security. This is a 
UNDP funded programme and my Ministry is the facili tator and the implementing 
agency is FRLHT. It is a centre of excellence in me dicinal plants. So far as 
Rajasthan is concerned, it is covered under this pr ogramme and necessary funding 
is made through this implementing agency. Regarding  herbal gardens, this is one 
of the components. Under this and through this sche me, funding is being made to 
the persons who desire to have a herbal garden.

*103. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be please d to 
state: 
(a) whether the Telecom Regulatory Authority of lndia (TRAI) Act which came into 
being in 1997 and in which many amendments have already been made, still has many 
shortcomings for which further amendments are required; 
(b) if so. whether the shortcomings have been indentified by Government; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) by when, necessary amendments are proposed to be made in the said Act? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (d) A Statement i s laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (c) TRAI Act, 1997 was amended once in Janua ry, 2000 by the Telecom 
Regulator, Authority of India (Amendment) Act. 2000. Subsequently a proposal has 
been received from TRAI for certain amendments to T RAI Act. 1997, to address 
various issues relating mainly to more operational freedom to TRAI and 
administration of broadcasting services. 
(d) The amendments proposed by TRAI in the TRAI Act . 1997 requires inter-
ministerial consultation before finalization of Government's views in this regard. No 
definite time-frame can, therefore, be given for ca rrying out the proposed 
amendment or otherwise. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir. one of the promises  made by the 
UPA Government, when it took office in 2004. was that it would review and strengthen 
the independent regulatory institutions, including telecom. The reason for this was 
obvious. It is clear that some of the regulatory institutions, more specifically, the one 
in telecom sector, have clearly not lived up to exp ectations in both, independence 
and quality. Unfortunately, very little has been do ne in this regard. Therefore, I 
would respectfully submit to the hon. Minister and push him for some specific 
answers. So, my first supplementary is that section 11 of the TRAI Act provides for 
an accord— "The authority shall ensure transparency  while exercising its powers 
in discharging its functions". I would submit that there is very little clarity on it 
really means vis-a-vis the responsibility of the TRAI. So, would the hon. Minister 
think it appropriate that the Act be amended to pro vide clarity on this section and 
to provide a stronger and more vigorous oversight of the Parliament on the TRAI. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, it is needless to submit before the House that 1 RAI is a 
Body which is constituted under a statute. Section 11 provides how the 
recommendations of the TRAI can be accepted and admitted by the Government as 
soon as it received the recommendations. So far as the recommendations made by 
the TRAI are concerned, most of the recommendations  were accepted by the 
Government. In case any deviation between the Ministry and the TRAI Regulator is 
there, the matter can be remitted to the TRAI by vi rtue of section 11. Such a case 
does not arise. If it arises, then, it will be remi tted back to the TRAI So, I do not 
think that, as such, section 11 needs any further amendment. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir, I would respectfully disagree with the 
Minister, but I hope that this can be further discu ssed. But, let me put a second 
supplementary which

Question No. 104. 
Grant of carbon credits to domestic companies 
*104. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA : †† 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has set up any national level me chanism to calculate 
and grant carbon credits to domestic companies; 
(b) whether Government have made any estimates of the p otential for domestic 
industry in carbon trade; 
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
(d) whether Government propose to hold capacity buildin g programme for the 
private and public industries in carbon trade? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (d) A Stat ement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (d) The Government of India has set up the N ational Clean Development 
Mechanism (CDM) Authority which is the designated N ational Authority for 
according Host Country Approval to eligible project s. Further validation of 
projects, including calculation of Certified Emissi on Reductions.(CERs), is 
undertaken by the Designated Operational Entities ( DOEs). Based on DOE 
recommendations, the Carbon Credits are issued by t he CDM Executive Board 
(EB), by following the stipulated procedure. 
As per National Strategy Study conducted in the yea r 200S, estimates of the 
potential for domestic industry with regard to gene ration of Certified Emission 
Reductions (CERs) are around 417 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent 
(MtC02eq) by the end of first commitment period of Kyoto Protocol i.e. 2012. 
Sector-wise break-up is as follows—Power generation  —319 MtC02eq, 
Transport—41 MtC02eq, Industries—57 MtC02eq. 
†† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shrimati Prema 
Cariappa.

collaboration with Asian Development Bank (ADB), wh ich has been well received 
by all stakeholders. The Government had also initia ted capacity building exercise 
with other multilateral agencies, viz. UNDP and GTZ, including capacity building 
of selected State level agencies.

*105. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be please d to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that two private telecom o perators have been found 
making false claims and drawing excess subsidy from  the Universal Service 
Obligation (USO) Fund for providing services in rural areas; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions   9 
(c) the steps taken by Government against them for making wrong subsidy 
claims? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) A Statement i s laid on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement  
(a) Errors have been identified in claims submitted by private and State owned 
service providers who have entered into agreements with Universal Service 
Obligation Fund (USOF). However, all such ineligibl e claims are disallowed at the 
time of claim verification stage itself or subseque ntly at the time of physical 
inspection. 
(b) The errors committed, inter-alia, are arithmetical mistakes, claims against 
faulty, disconnected and closed connections and cla ims for connections ineligible 
areas. 
(c) Following steps are taken with reference to ine ligible claims:— 
(i) All such ineligible claims on detection are disallowed. 
(ii) Based upon implementation experience, the method of claim verification is 
continuously improved for ongoing as well as new activities undertaken by USOF. 
SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Sir, I would like to know f rom the hon. 
Minister what efforts are being made by the Government to take telecom revolution 
to the villages in our country. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the question relates to the Univ ersal Service Obligation 
Fund under which rural telephony and rural tele-density is being improved. 
Sir, in terms of financial achievements, right from  the year 2002-03, when the 
USO Fund came into existence with a statutory statu s, so far, the funds 
accumulated, which are non-lapsable, amount to Rs. 14,999 crores. Out of these Rs. 
14,999 crores, till date, Rs. 5375 crores have been  released upto 30th September, 
2007 and a further approximately Rs. 5,000 crores have been earmarked for ongoing 
activities. Out of these funds, the major works being carried out by the Ministry are: 
operation and maintenance of village public telephones, that is, Provision of Village 
public telephones have in the villages where accessibility of telephones has not been 
given to the very remote villages installation of r ural community phones and 
installation of rural direct exchange lines and shared infrastructure for mobile services. 
These are the major activities being carried out by  the USO Fund, the Universal 
Service Obligation Fund. 
In terms of physical achievement, other operators w ere permitted to participate 
in the achievement of the goal. So far, the physical achievement that has been made 
under the USO Fund is the replacement of MARR (Multi-Access Radio Relay) with 
VPTs. Since it is a comparatively old technology, Government wanted to replace the 
MARR technology with VPTs on reliable technology. S o far, 1,79,365 VPTs have 
been replaced out of 1,82,766 MARR VPTs. 
In the other provisions, for rural community phones , so far, through BSNL and 
Reliance, we have provided 37,786 rural community phones out of 43409 RCPs. In 
terms of RDEL (Rural Direct Exchange Lines), so far , about 25 lakh RDELs have 
been provided in 1685 Cost Positive SPCAs. So, in t erms of physical achievement 
and financial achievement also, we are going to giv e fullest rural telephony in the 
near future.

SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, I would like to know from 
the hon. Minister, since there is lot of migration to the towns, people are migrating in 
large numbers to the towns, population in urban are as is increasing drastically year 
after year. So, it is very difficult for local bodi es, town committees to provide 
water, sanitation, housing, power, for that. I woul d like to know whether any study 
has been conducted regarding migration from rural areas to urban areas, necessities in 
urban areas, and fund position with the local bodie s. Is there any proposal with the 
Government of India for extending financial support to the local bodies for acquiring 
land to provide house sites to the poor people who cannot afford to purchase a 
house site in the urban area? 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: The question is specifically on JNNURM funds for Andhra 
Pradesh. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: My question was wh ether 
sufficient funds are provided to the State of Andhra Pradesh for providing amenities 
for the people in urban areas. I think, it is part of my question. 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: I would like to tell the hon. Member that the whole concept 
of Urban Renewal Mission is to provide the urban local bodies with sufficient funds 
and simultaneously, to carry out reforms in urban l ocal bodies so that they are 
financially strong enough and viable enough to sustain with the funds which we are 
providing, so that all the projects become sustainable. 
As far as the water supply and other important thin gs, as raised by the hon. 
Member, are concerned, I would like to tell that water supply, sanitation and sewage, 
these are all areas where 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions    13 
we are giving prime importance. He would be glad to know that under UIDSSMT, 60 per 
cent of the total money is given for the water supply, and 17 per cent for the sewage. So, 
water supply and sewage are being given adequate importance. As far as Andhra Pradesh is 
concerned, I would like to tell that in the last two years alone, under UIDSSMT, we have 
been able to give Rs. 235.46 crores, and under UIG we have been able to give Rs. 137.31 
crores on all such projects. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, my question was regarding migration 
from the rural areas to the urban areas. Is there any study done in that regard? While coming 
to my second supplementary question, I leave it to the hon. Minister if he chooses to 
answer my first question, I will be happy; otherwise, I won't mind. Sir, as far as second 
part of my question is concerned, I have the details of the schemes sanctioned for my own 
State, Andhra Pradesh, and I would like to know fro m the hon. Minister about the 
proposals sent by the Government of Andhra Pradesh with regard to Urban infrastructure and 
Governance (UIG) and Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small and Medium 
Towns (UIDSSMT). I would like to know how many projects are sanctioned and how 
many are pending. Is there any time-frame for that? 
SHRI AJAY MAKEN: Sir, I would like to tell the hon. Member that as far as Urban 
Infrastructure and Governance is concerned, in total, 33 projects have been approved. As far as 
projects under appraisal are concerned, only two projects are pending with the Central 
Government for appraisal. As far as projects returned to the State of Andhra Pradesh for 
modification are concerned, in total 38 projects have been send back to them for modification 
because different objections have been raised by the appraisal agencies. As far as UIDSSMT 
projects are concerned, 52 projects are pending because already we have sanctioned and 
released much more amount than what was due for the State of Andhra Pradesh. So, the 
projects, which are pending under the UIDSSMT, are pending because Andhra Pradesh has 
already got the money which is more than its share. 
As far as migration of population to urban areas is concerned, I would like to tell the 
hon. Member that now around 30 per cent of our population lives in the urban areas. It is 
envisaged that by the year 2025, another 10 to 15 per cent of our population will be in 
urban areas. So, all our attention, through JNNURM, is to satisfy the migrated propulation 
as wall as those who are already living in the urban areas.
