Settlement of claims under PLIS 
*108. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHL : †† 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has fixed any maximum time limit within which death claims must 
be settled under the Postal Life Insurance Scheme (PLIS); 
(b) if so, the number of claims settled within this time limit; and 
(c) the average time taken for different death claims settled under the Postal Life Insurance 
Scheme (PLIS) during the last three years? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
† [Transliteration in Urdu Script.] 
†† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Gireesh Kumar Sanghi. 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV. 2007]  to Questions    15 
Statement  
(a) Yes, Sir. A time limit of 60 days from the actual d ate of receipt of complete 
papers is the norms except in those cases where inv estigation into the bonafides of 
the claim is required. 
(b) In the current year, 2007, 5790 claims have been se ttled till 31.10.07 within 
this time limit where all claims received were complete and no investigation into the 
bonafides of the claim was required. 
(c) The average time taken for death claims settled during last three years is 20 days 
in cases where claims were received with complete papers and no investigation was 
required. 
SHRl GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: Sir, I would like to ask the hon. Minister as 
to how many cases are pending; and if so, what is t he time-schedule by which they 
will be settled; and what are the steps that the Pe rsonnel Department is taking to 
ensure that all the information required is collect ed initially; and if there is any 
proposal to keep all the pending cases on the internet the details of queries raised; and 
what are the advantages of the Postal Life Insuranc e vis-a-vis in comparison with 
LIC and other service-providers; and how the bonus is decided. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, so far, 5,790 claims have been s ettled within the statutory 
period contemplated in the rules. Only 704 cases ar e pending for disposal. The 
reason behind the pendency is, there are two catego ries in case of death or in case 
of maturity or in case of surrender. In case of dea th, if it is within three years from 
the date of policy, then, according to the law, fur ther investigation must be done 
regarding the cause of death and other things. If i t is after three years, we have no 
problem, we will scrutinise the documents. lt it is  within three years, some 
investigation is needed according to the procedure contemplated in the law. Because the 
procedure is being followed for investigation, it is being delayed. There is no delay at 
all on the part of the Department. 
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: Sir, he has not replied to my other question 
which is whether these queries will be put on the I nternet. What are the queries 
raised; what are the advantages of the Postal Life Insurance vis-a-vis the LIC; and 
how is the bonus decided? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the question of getting claims i s right in persona. So, the 
Department feels that it need not be put on the web site. It relates only to the person 
who is having contract with the Department. 
With regard to bonus, it is calculated on the basis  of the position of the fund and 
the mortality rate among the applicants. Subject to  this, bonus is being given. But I 
can assure you that whatever is being given by the Postal Life Insurance is definitely 
higher than the Life Insurance Corporation. 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, the Postal Life Insurance is being taken by the 
poorest of the poor people. Actually, they are very  poor people and they do not 
have the proper infrastructure. Sir, I would like t o know from the hon. Minister if 
the papers are not complete in all respects would h e like to have a separate officer 
there who can help them complete the papers in one go. Sir, what are the norms in 
respect of after-sale services for the policy? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the significance and importance attached with the Postal Life 
Insurance is something unique when it is compared t o the other insurance systems. 
The operational cost of the Postal Life Insurance i s much lower than the other 
insurance companies. The reasons behind this is, al most in 1,50,000 villages, towns 
and semi-towns, they are having post offices either in the name of Extra Departmental 
Post Office or the Sub-Post Office or Head Post Office whatever be the nomenclature 
of the post office. The infrastructure available ac ross the country is giving very 
efficient service and it is very beneficial to the people. So, using the network, it is

*109.  SHRI MOHAMMED AMIN: 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: †† 
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any mechanism or supervisory body to ensure that the 
contracts between Indian workers in Middle-East cou ntries and the contractors and 
employers are adhered to; 
(b) if so, the number of cases of violations that have been reported in the years 
2006 and 2007 and the steps that have been taken to  redress their grievances/breach 
of contracts; and 
(c) if not, the steps that are being taken to take care  of growing number of cases 
being reported about breach of contracts, under-pay ment, ill-treatment like seizure 
of passport, etc. and poor working conditions? 
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS (SHRI VAYAL AR 
RAVI): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
†† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Prasanta 
Chatterjee. 

Oral Answers  [22 NOV.2007]  to Questions   17 
Statement  
(a) Yes, Sir. The Protector General of Emigrants (PGE) is the statutory authority 
designated 
under the Emigration Act, 1983 for the protection and welfare of emigrants. 
The work contract between the employer and the work er set out the terms and 
conditions of employment, violation of which attracts the penal provisions of the Act. 
In the case of unskiled workers/household service workers the work contracts has to 
be duly attested by the Embassy of India. The Recru iting Agent is liable to ensure 
compliance of the terms and conditions of the contract on the part of the employer. 
In the event of violation of the contractual provis ions, action is taken against the 
recruiting agent by way of suspension/cancellation of the license and/or prosecution. 
The Foreign Employers (FEs) concerned are blacklisted. 
In order to reinforce this regulatory system and to  ensure that contractual 
obligations are adhered to by the employer and for the protection and welfare of the 
workers, the Ministry has signed bilateral agreemen ts with major labour receiving 
countries. Such MOUs have been signed with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and 
Kuwait. An Additional Protocol has been signed with Qatar. MOU has been finalised 
with Malaysia and Oman. These agreements provide fo r a Joint Working Group to 
look into and resolve the problems and concerns of Indian workers including 
adherence of the terms and conditions of work contracts by employers.

them have been put behind bars since they were dema nding justice from their

That is my first question. 
SHRI VAYALAR RAVI: Sir, deportation is done on two reasons. Large number 
of workers have been deported because they were on illegal stay there. They were

Sir, the other question is that recently there was some agitation in some institutions of 
one of the Gulf countries. I think, those who were involved in violence there — 159 people 
— have been detained. Out of these, 90 are Indian n ationals. They were detained and 
arrested, but, due to the intervention or persuasion of our Mission, 90 have been deported. In 
the same way, in another company, there was a strik e. About 500 people have been 
detained and not all of them are Indian nationals; there are other nationals also. All the 500 
have been deported. That is the story. Another important thing is, to protect the interests 
of the workers, the Ministry has taken initiatives. We have already signed a Memorandum 
of Understanding with Kuwait as well as UAE. We hav e stipulated the protection of 
workers' salary, medical benefits, living conditions including the domestic workers and 
women workers. Two days ago, I signed an agreement with Qatar in the same way. Now, 
initial negotiations have been completed with two other countries, that is, Bahrain and 
Oman. I am trying to persuade the Government of the State of Saudi Arabia to come to the 
negotiating table to make this kind of an agreement. We are taking care of the workers' 
interests and  we will continue to do that. 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Sir, my second question i s that some 
unauthorised agents are operating in the field. A l arge number of such agnecies are 
existing in Indian who have been identified as unau thorised agency houses. So, I 
want to know from the Government: What action has b een taken by the 
Government so far to check their illegal activities? 
SHRI VAYALAR RAVI: Sir, it is a very important question. The Government is 
taking all the steps. It is true that a large numbe r of unauthorised people, claim to be 
agents, are going to the villages and exploiting the poor people. Sir, if you can taken 
the complaints of the last three years, it comes to  53 for 2005,78 for 2006 and so far 
37 complaints in this year. Prosecution has also be en recommended. Sir, action has 
to be taken by the State Governments. We are pursui ng with the State Governments 
to take very stringent action. Prosecution must be pusued with all vigour. That is the 
only way. Now, there is proposal to amend the Immig ration Act. It will definitely 
go for the consideration of the Cabinet. I can assu re this House that after the 
amendment is passed, we will do our best to check t his problem in collaboration 
with the State Government. With their help, we can do that. I hope all the State 
Governments will cooperate with us in checking these unauthorised activities.

Usage and disposal of mercury  
*113. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be p leased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has initiated any instructio n/guidelines to the 
private and Government hospitals for usage and disp osal of mercury, because the 
minimal risk level for mercury of 0.2 micro gram, but in hospitals the mercury level 
is forty times higher than the normal limit which l eads to neuro-developmental 
disorders in newborns; 
(b) if so, whether there is any environmental authority  to monitor such level to 
save staff, including doctors and paramedical employees and patients; 
(c) the protective measures taken in this behalf; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (d) Improp er handling and 
breakage of instruments containing mercury contaminates the solid waste generated in 
hospitals and can cause environmental pollution. 
Guidelines for proper collection and disposal of th e spilled mercury have been 
circulated by the Central Pollution Control Board ( CPCB) to all State Pollution 
Control Boards (SPCBs), Pollution Control Committee s (PCCs) in Union 
Territories and other conterned agencies. The CPCB has also issued instructions to 
all the SPCBs and PCCs that mercury spillages/losse s in health care facilities need 
to be given proper attention so that spilled mercur y is collected and sent back to the 
manufacturers, and measures are taken to ensure tha t the spilled mercury does not 
become part of the bio-medical or other solid waste  generated from the healthcare 
facilities. Any waste containing equal to or greate r than 50 ppm or mercury is 
categorized as hazardous waste as per the Hazardous  Wastes (Management & 
Handling) Rules, 2003 and healthcare facilities are  required to dispose of such 
wastes in accordance with the said Rules. The SPCBs / PCCs have also been 
requested to bring this aspect/requirement to the notice of the healthcare facilities and 
ensure incorporation of appropriate conditions in the authorizations granted by them 
under the Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, 1998. 
No ill effects of mercury in any Central Government  Hospital have come to the 
notice of the Government.

(c) While Thorium by itself cannot serve as a fuel for generating power in a

India has formulated a three stage nuclear power pr ogramme to optimally use its 
modest uranium and vast thorium resources to fulfil  the increasing energy 
requirements of the country. Large scale thorium ut ilization is contemplated in the 
third stage of this programme, where Uranium-233 br ed in fast breeder reactors of 
the second stage, will be used together with thoriu m. The Government has taken a 
number of steps to develop appropriate technologies for the utilization of thorium. A 
few of the major steps are: 
(1) Setting up the research reactor Kamini at Kalpakkam using Uranium-233 fuel 
obtained from irradiated thorium. The reactor has been operating since 1997. 
The fuel for the reactor is bred, reprocessed and fabricated indigenously.

earth compounds which are recovered from monazite. 30,000 (thirty thousand) tonnes

1434.      SHRI MOTILAL VORA: 
SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION  
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Electromagnetic Radiation  (EMR) always continue 
from mobile phone towers; 
(b) if so, the effects of EMR on human body; 
(c) the rules regarding setting up of mobile phone towers; 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(e) the time by when rules will be framed in this direction; and 
(0 whether Government will arrange for strict monitoring till the rules are framed 
in this regard?   . 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICAT IONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a)  to (f) 
Yes, Sir. The electromagnetic radiations are always  present from any antenna 
emitting radio signals, whether it is a mobile phon e tower or a broadcast tower etc. 
The level of electromagnetic radiations within safe ty limits is harmless. The latest 
Fact Sheet of World Health Organisation (WHO) (No. 304 of May, 2006) states that 
from all evidence accumulation so far, no adverse s hort or long-term health effects 
have been shown to occur from the RF signals produc ed by base station. Since 
wireless networks produce generally lower RF signals than base stations, no adverse 
health effects are expected exposure to them. Further, a Committee was setup under 
the Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), as per the orders 
of Hon'ble High Court, Mumbai, to study the effects  of radiations from mobile 
phone towers and related aspects. The Committee had  studied the effects and 
concluded that overall there is not enough evidence to show direct health hazards of 
RF exposures from mobile base stations.

Melting of Gomukh Glacier 
 447. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Gomukh glacier, the origin of Gangotri (river Ganges) is melting 
and slowly vanishing; 
(b) if so, details thereof and reasons therefor; 
(c) its impact on the availability of water during next two decades; and 
(d) the steps being taken to save and restore the existence of Gomukh glacier? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) The studies carried out by Department of 
Science and Technology on Gangotri Glacier have revealed that the Glacier was receding at the 
rate of 17.15 m/year during 1971-2004 period. Another study estimated a retreat of 12.10 m 
during the year 2004-05. Compilations of the data on secular movement of glaciers have revealed 
that the majority of the glaciers of the Himalayan region are passing through a phase of recession, 
which is a worldwide phenomenon. The causative factors for this variable retreat may be 
subnormal snowfall, higher temperature during summer, less severe winter or a combination of 
all of them. It could also be attributed to the phenomenon of rise in temperature, global warming, 
to some extent. 
(c) The Government has not undertaken any study to correlate the river discharge, water 
level changes in sea and ocean and the recession of the glaciers. In addition to the glaciers, 
seasonal snow cover, groundwater and rainfall contribute to the river discharge. Due to enhanced 
melting of ice, consequent upon faster recession, the runoff of the Himalayan rivers may 
increase marginally. 
(d) The recession of glaciers cannot be prevented on a large scale in view of the nature of 
Indian Himalayan Glaciers being debris covered, the economic feasibility, the scale of operation 
and the likelihood of pollution. As the prime responsibility of reducing emissions that enhance 
global warming lies with the developed countries, the Government of India has been pressing in 
international negotiations that these countries should take deeper emission reduction commitments 
and for a longer period.

National policy for global warming  
465. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR Will the PRIME MINIS TER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulate a new national po licy for addressing the 
issue of global warming; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, by when that is likely to be done? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) The N ational 
Environment Policy 2006 of Ministry of Environment & Forests inter alia 
addresses the issue of global warming. The followin g comprise essential elements 
of India's response to climate change: 
(1) Adherence to the principle of common but differenti ated responsibilities 
and respective capabilities of different countries in respect of both 
mitigation of green house gases (GHGs), an adaptation measures. 
(2) Reliance on multilateral approaches, as opposed to bilateral or plurilateral or 
unilateral measures. 
(3) Equal per-capita entitlements of global environmental resources to all 
countries. 
(4) Over-riding priority of the right to development. 
(5) Identify key vulnerabilities of India to climate change, in particular impacts 
on water resources, forests coastal areas, agricultre, and health. 
(6) Assess the need for adaptation to future climate ch ange, and the scope for 
incorporating these in relevant programmes, including watershed management, 
coastal zone planning and regulation; forestry mana gement, agricultural 
technologies and practices, and health programmes. 
(7) Encourage Indian Industry to participate in the Cle an Development 
Mechanism (CDM) through capacity building for ident ifying and 
preparing CDM projects, including in the financial sector 
(8) Participate in voluntary partnerships with other co untries both developed 
and developing, to address the challanges of sustai nable development and 
climate change, consistent with the provisions of t he UN Framework 
Convention on Climate Change. 
Further, the Government has also set up "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate 
Change" in May 2007 to study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India 
and to identify the measures that we may have to ta ke in the future in relation to 
addressing vulnerability to anthropogenic climate change impacts. 
Acoordination committee chaired by Hon'ble Prime Mi nister called "Prime 
Minister's Council on Climate Change to coordinate national action for assessment, 
adaptation and mitigation of climate change" was constituted on 6th June 2007. The 
focus of the Committee would be to: 
I. Evolve a coordinated response to issues relating to climate change at the 
national level; 
II. Provide oversight for formulation of action plans in the area of assessment, 
adaptation and mitigation of climate change; 
III.  Periodically monitor key policy decisons.

Statement  
Details regarding scheme for giving Legal/Financial Assistance to women 
deserted by theirOverseas Indian Spouses  
I. Objective: 
The objective of the scheme is to provide some fina ncial assistance to needy 
women in distress who have been deserted by their O verseas Indian spouses for 
obtaining counseling and legal services. The term " Overseas Indian" would include 
NRIs and foreign citizens of Indian origin. The cou nseling and legal services would 
be provided through credible Indian Women's Organiz ations/Indian Community 
Associations and NGOs identified for providing such  services and empanelled with 
the Indian Missions in the USA, the UK, Canada, Aus tralia, New Zealand and the 
Gulf. The scheme is a welfare measure to support wo men of Indian origin in 
distress, through the mobilization of the local Ind ian community in the endeavour 
and with some financial assistance from the Governm ent. 
II. Scope of and eligibility for the Scheme: 
The scheme would be available to the women who have  been deserted by their 
overseas Indian spouses or are facing divorce proce edings in a foreign country 
subject to the following conditions:— 

72    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(i) The woman is an Indian passport holder. 
(ii) The marriage of the woman has been solemnized in India. 
(iii) The woman is deserted in India or after reach ing abroad within five years 
of the marriage. 
(iv) Divorce proceedings are initiated within five years of the marriage by her 
overseas Indian spouse. 
(v) An ex-parte divorce has been obtained by the overseas Indian spouse within 
ten years of the marriage and a case for maintenanc e and alimony is to be 
filed. 
(vi) The scheme would not be available to a woman f acing criminal charges or 
having a criminal case decided against her. 
(vii) The domicile of the woman seeking relief under the scheme is not relevant for 
allowing the benefit. The woman may be domiciled in  the country of her 
overseas Indian spouse or in India at the time of making the application. 
(viii) Preference may be given to applicants on the basis of financial needs. 
(ix) Assistance will be limited to meeting initial cost and incidental charges for 
documentation and filing of the case by the Indian women's 
organization/NGO on the woman's behalf. 
(x) The assistance will be limited to US $ 1000 per case and will be released to 
the Indian community organizations/NGO concerned to  enable it to take 
steps to assist the woman in documentation and prep aratory work for filing 
the case. 
(xi) The women's organization/NGO will make efforts  to enlist community 
advocates, preferably women advocates, to extend fu rther legal 
assistance/appearance in court etc. on a pro-bono basis. 
Pattern of Assistance 
Under the scheme Indian Missions in the countries c oncerned would empanel 
credible Indian Women's Organizations/Indian Community Associations/NGOs and 
their member advocates, preferably women, to provid e legal aid to the victims in 
distress and whose names have been approved by the Ministry of Overseas Indian 
Affairs. The applications for providing legal aid r eceived by the Missions would by 
examined by an officer designated by the Head of th e Mission on case-to-case basis 
and approved by Head of Mission/Deputy Chief of the Mission. 
The applications received in the Ministry of Overse as Indian Affairs will be 
examined by an internal committee consisting of a legal advisor and an officer of the 
rank of Director/Deputy Secretary and approved by S ecretary. Thereafter, the 
Ministry will recommend the case to Mission concern ed to provide legal aid 
support. The applicant would also be informed to ap proach the Mission concerned 
in this regard.

recommended the scrapping of the Official Secret Act;

regard;

wake of the RTI Act coming into force; and

GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): (a)  to (d) The

Master Key to Good Governance" has inter alia recommended that the Official 
Secrets Act (OSA), 1923 should be repealed and subs tituted by a chapter in the 
National Security Act, containing provisions relati ng to official secrets. It has also 
recommended that the existing section 5 of the Offi cial Secret Act may be 
reformulated on the lines recommended by the Shourie Committee. The OSA is the 
only law on the statute book to deal with cases of espionage and wrongful possession 
and communication of sensitive information detrimental to security of the State. This 
law has stood

(a) whether Government are aware that poverty alleviati on programmes in India 
have not been able to create a balanced impact and there are still a large number of

National waterways 
497. SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: 
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to develop two new national waterways in West Bengal-Orissa 
and Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also proposed to prepare a road map for an integrated transport to include 
inland water transport, coastal shipping, civil aviation, road transport and highways for enabling 
better inter-connectivity among multi-modes of transport; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI TR. 
BAALU): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) A proposal to declare Kakinada-Puducherry stretch of canals consisting of Kakinada 
canal, Eluru canal, Commannur canal, Buckingham canal and Kaluvelly tank along with 
Bhadrachalam—Rajahmundry stretch of River Godavari and Wazirabad—Viyayawada stretch 
of River Krishna (1095 kms.) as a National Waterway is under consideration of the Govt. This 
Waterway System is in the States of Andhra Pradesh, and Tamilnadu and Union Territory of 
Puducherry. The Bill for enacting Central Legislation was introduced on 08.12.2006. It was 
referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture for 
examination. The Parliamentary Standing Committee has recently submitted its report. Follow 
up action is being taken. The total estimated cost of the project is Rs. 542 cr. (at 2002 prices). 
Similarly, a proposal to declare Geonkhali-Charbatia stretch of East Coast Canal 
(217 km.) along with Charbatia-Dhamra stretch of Matai river (40 km), Talcher-Dhamra 
stretch of River Brahmani (265 km.) and Mangalgadi-Paradip stretch of Mahanadi delta rivers 
(101 km.) in the States of West Bengal and Orissa as a National Waterway is also under 
consideration of the Government. The bill for enacting Central legislation for this waterway 
was introduced in the Parliament on 08.12.2006. It was referred to the Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture for examination. The Parliamentary Standing 
Committee has recently submitted its report. Follow up action is being taken. The total 
estimated cost of this project is Rs. 1526 cr. (at 2002 prices). 
(c) and (d) Planning commission has entrusted Rail India Technical and Economic Services 
(RITES) with the task of conducting a total Transport System Study with a view to generating 
and analysing inter-modal transport resource costs and traffic flows, covering the four major 
mechanized modes of transport—Railways, Highways, Airways and Shipping and determining 
an optimal inter-modal mix and allocation of transport investment.

(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. A research project R-64 entitled "Establishment of System for 
Identification and Rectification of Accident Black Spots" was undertaken by this 
Ministry in the year 1995. 18 selected sections of 100m each on 15NHs were 
considered in the study. 
Based on accident analysis, the following conclusio ns have been drawn with 
regards to road accidents, their causes, occurrence s, causalities and vehicle 
improvement. 
(i) Maximum number of accidents, especially fatal a ccidents are found to 
occur on straight stretches due to high speed. 
(ii) Four arm junctions were found to be most vulne rable mainly due to 
insufficient site distance, lack of traffic guidance, absence of road markings 
and poor road geometries. 
(iii) Head on collisions are found to be maximum du e to high speed and bad 
overtaking practice. 
(iv) Pedestrians are most vulnerable victims due to  insufficient pedestrian 
facilities and poor knowledge of about traffic rule s. Pedestrians are ranked 
second in making errors and one of the main causes of accidents. 
(v) Driver error is found to be main causes by many accidents. 
(vi) Maximum number of causalities are observed by car, followed by 
pedestrians and then by heavy goods vehicles. 
(vii) During night time trucks are involved in maximum numbers of accidents. 
(viii) The share of negligence and over-speeding in accidents is found to be as high 
as 90%.

departmentally executed projects;

Procedure for selection for Arjuna Awards  
526. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister o f YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the procedure for recommendation/nomination of candidates eligible for the Arjuna 
Awards; 
(b) the procedure followed after the nominations/recommendations have been made 
to select awardees; 
(c) the reason for games like tennis and carom, not being enlisted in drawing 
awardees; and 
(d)the steps taken to make the selection process mo re encompassing of other 
sports and also more transparent in its working? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) The eligibility criteria for th e Arjuna Awards includes 
consistently good performance for the previous thre e years at international level 
coupled with leadership and sportspersonship qualities. The award is considered in 
both Olympic and Non-Olympic disciplines, including  indigenous games and 
sports for the physically challenged. Nominations f or the award are invited from 
recognized National Sports Federations, the Indian Olympic Association, State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations and Sports Control/Promotion Boards 
of various Government organizations such as Police, Army etc. 
(b) The nominations received are duly scrutinized and e ligible nominations are 
placed before an independent selection committee co nsisting of eminent 
sportspersons, including Olympians and past Arjuna Awardees, Government 
representatives and sports administrators. The Selection Committee determines its own 
work procedure and the selection is made by consens us failing which by a majority 
decision. 
(c) and (d) While all disciplines including Tennis and Carom are considered for the 
award, the Selection Committee selects the awardees on the basis of their performance 
at major international events. Since ordinarily not more than 15 awards are given in a 
particular year, it is not possible to cover all sports disciplines every year. In the past, 
several Tennis players have been conferred Arjuna Awards such as S/Shri Ramnathan 
Krishnan, Jaideep Mukherjee, Vijay Amritraj, Ramesh

Krishnan, Anand Amritraj, Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhup ati, Akhtar Ali, Ms. Sania 
Mirza, etc. Similarly, in Carom, Sh. Anthony Maria Irudayam was conferred the 
Arjuna Award.

That we have recaptured Nandigram by force. Sir, ou r people have gone back to 
Nandigram. Our people, who are the legitimate owner s of their houses, have gone 
back to their houses. Our people, who till those la nds, have gone back to their own 
lands. The children have gone back to their own hom es. And the children, who were 
denied schooling are now restarting their life after one year. Is it a crime for people to 
go back to their homes? Is it a crime for farmers t o go back to till their lands? If they 
are charging us that we have done this through force, I am saying that we have done 
this by resisting the force, not. by employing force; the force was employed from the 
other side. We have resisted that and gone back to our homes. And for 11 months, 
when they were deprived of their homes, when they w ere thrown out as refugees

petroleum investment region. Yes, there was a propo sal there for a chemical hub.

acquired, but, no formal land acquisition notice was ever issued. There was a notice

happened in Nandigram is actually a direct political challenge to destabilise an elected 
Government there, and, that is precisely the logical conclusion that they all want ftflead 
up to seeking imposing President's Rule there. The destablisation of an elected Government—
if this is permitted by the use of extremist forces and Maoist violence—is something that is 
not in the interest of India; forget West Bengal, forget CPI (M). We are playing with fire. If you 
are stoking them and actually patronizing and supporting them in order to settle Petty political 
scores here and there, you are actually playing with the future of the entire country. So, 
Nandigram is an abject lesson for -.»!! of us. All this evidence that I have given shows how 
the Maoists penetrated, how they ha - gone into each of those villages, and, how they 
themselves mocked at the Trinamool

declaration of an armed action against an Indian State. If this is ignored, if that is not

Therefore, with the responsibility that is required  of all of us, we will have to take 
up this issue in the larger context. People who had  actually been driven out of their 
homes have gone back to their homes, as I said, not  by using force but by resisting.

can only ignore at our peril and that larger issue must be kept in mind. Do not reduce 
it only to settle petty political scores. Keep the interest of India in mind. 
This is the appeal that we have to make. I want to asure this august House that as 
far as CPI (M) is concerned, with the fullest confi dence and commitment to the 
democracy that we have shown all these years and wh ich we will continue to show, 
we do not want this process to be undermined. These  forces must be put to check, 
and, that is my sincere appeal. Thank you.

SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Now I'm speaking in Bengali again. Sir, I want to conclude 
with a couplet written by Rabindranath Tagore. Brin daji, you have been singing this 
song for long but might have forgotten now. The song follows like this: 
If you create obstacles, the struggle will ensue and we may have to court death. 
If you block the road, you have to clear the way. 
You want to become rich with the wealth accumulated by looting. 
You will fall on the dusty road just in a minute. 
If you want to shake it, you will also be shaken. 

172   Short Duration [RAJYA SABHA] Discussion  
[SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA] 
If you create obstacles, the struggle will ensue and we may have to court death. 
You have to accept the truth. And please tell the Chief Minister who says, "An eye 
for an eye", that this is not the way. If you want to win over the people, you should 
work on other ways, but not this way. And please al so arrange for their 
rehabilitation. Thank you, Sir. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, we have been discussing since noon 
time about the issue of Special Economic Zones, spe cially Nandigram, and 
consequential violence in that area. Sir, there are two distinct things—one is Special 
Economic Zones and the other part is violence in Na ndigram. Sir, this is an 
unfortunate incident in Nandigram and going by the newspaper reports and going by 
the speeches, I feel that one should express sympat hy to the victims. The 
Government should.take all the steps for rehabilita tion and extending financial 
assistance for all the victims and we should see that normalcy is restored at the earliest. 
Sir, main cause for all these incidents and events,  which are avoidable, is Special 
Economic Zones. The Government of India, as of now, have sanctioned 375 Special 
Economic Zones. Sir, the very purpose is defeated. Sir, going by the trends in the 
country, going by the resistance from land owners, small and marginal farmers, it is 
going to end up as a displaced development and as m isplaced priority. I feel that in 
the name of SEZ, many people, who are close to ruli ng dispensations in various 
States, are floating all the economic zones. We are  aware of the concessions given 
to these Special Economic Zones, specially tax exemptions, duty free import, domestic 
procurement of goods for development, hundred per c ent income tax exemption, 
exemption from minimum alternate tax, exemption from Central sales tax, service tax, 
single window clearance for all these economic zone s etc. For whose benefits, they 
are floating these Special Economic Zones. The Government should have a thorough 
review of these economic zones. In my own State, An dhra Pradesh, 70 Special 
Economic Zones have been cleared. Sir, 25,000 acres of land is going to be acquired, 
and, most of them are already floated there in the State. And, Sir, people who are very 
close to the Ruling Party are floating these Special Economic Zones. Sir, information 
technology companies are also acquiring lands in th e name of Special Economic 
Zones. The concessions are given to the entrepreneurs, and, more than fifty per cent 
concession is availed for real estate purposes. Why  should the Government of India 
or the respective State Government act as middlemen  in acquiring the lands? Sir, 
literally, they have become real estate brokers. 
Sir, now, the land has become very precious, and, in the name of SEZ, people are 
grabbing the agriculture lands. Sir, already, when the cultivable land is shrinking in 
the country and the agricultural production is also  coming down, we are encouraging 
Special Economic Zones in the agricultural fields. Sir, a day will come when instead of 
earmarking Special Economic Zones, we will have to earmark certain land for special 
agricultural fields. Sir, we can call the present SEZs as 'special encroachment zones' 
into the agriculture fields and thereby becoming special exploitation zones. They are 
literally exploiting the fields. 
Sir, the concept of SEZ has to be throughly reviewed. There should be an evaluation. 
Sir, I am having the data with me. Due to paucity of time, I cannot give all the details.

above these things. Sir, the first aspect which I w ish to draw the attention of this 
august House to is the debates when our Constitutio n was being formulated. When 
our Constitution was being formulated in the Consti tuent Assembly, there was a 
debate at some length as to how and how much and what to give to the States in terms 
of Constitutional power. We, ultimately, ended up with the First List of the Constitution 
which is extremely large and very voluminous. The t erritory and the area covered by 
the First List of the Seventh Schedule is, in proportion, much larger than the State List 
or the Concurrent List. That is why from being a fully federal Constitution, we are called 
a quasi-federal Constitution. But, even in that debate— because our founders were 
concerned about the possible break-up of this natio n, about the fissiparous 
tendencies which beset the nation at that time in the context of partition—there was a 
very strong move to say that law and order is somet hing which we must give to the 
States; law and order is something which must be given in the widest possible meaning 
and amplitude to the States because we cannot have the beginning of federalism 
unless we gave law and order, not only as a word, but in spirit and in an enlarged zone 
also to the States. And, that is why, in the

Second List for the States, the first entry is law and order. Even in certain aspects, 
of what the Supreme Court has called the three concentric circles—the narrower circle 
is law and order, the slightly larger circle is pub lic order and the largest circle, is the 
security of the State—the security of the State, th e largest concentric circle, may be 
given and has been given to the Centre. But, the entirety of law and order, and in that 
connected sense, large parts of public order were d eliberately, after much debate, 
much comments by the framers, given to the States. There is a reason for it. And, it is 
for that reason, every State Government—1 don't mean this only for West Bengal, but

THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): There are a number of speakers. 
Hereafter each hon. Member will take five minutes or maximum seven minutes and not more 
than that. 
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY (Karnataka): Up to what time will we sit? 
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): That is why I said that each hon. 
Member would take five minutes or maximum seven minutes. 
DR. BARUN MUKHERJEE (West Bengal): Sir, thank you very much for the 
opportunity given to me. At the same time, there is a stricture that we should restrict our time. 
Sir, all of us know that the problem in Nandigram started with the proposal of SEZ. At 
the outset, I should say, on behalf of my party, the All India Forward Block, that we are 
opposed to this SEZ, as we think that it is the biggest land grab move during the recent times in 
the name of promoting exports, in the name of industrialisation. All this is being done to favour 
a few corporate houses, and some foreign houses, at the cost of millions of poor farmers. It will 
not only affect our food security, but it will also affect the livelihood of millions of poor farmers. So, 
we are firmly against this SEZ policy. And, as it has been noticed, irrespective of political 
affiliations, there has been resistance to SEZs in many other States of the country because the 
poor farmers have felt a pinch that if the farmland is lost, then, everything is lost. So, in spite of our 
representation to the Central Government, unfortunately, this has been rejected and all these 
things are going on. And we also find that the Government of India is merrily giving more and 
more approvals to SEZs; it is apprehended that it may touch tlie figure of thousand within a 
couple of months. So, we are basically opposed to SEZs. The same thing happened when a 
proposal came for establishing an SEZ at Nandigram. Naturally, there was a hue and cry over it. 
We are of the opinion that before the announcement of the SEZ, perhaps, proper homework was 
not done. I can even say, without mentioning the name of anybody, a top-ranking leader of the 
State, during out internal meeting, admitted that they did find afterwards that this acquisition 
would not only cover the farmlands, but also temples, mosques and graveyards. These are all 
being included there. So, there was a panic amongst people. But, unfortunately, this was made 
a political issue and, very quickly, some committee, in the name of Bhumi Uchhed Pratirodh

Sir, I fully endorse Shri Madani's stand—whenever we speak against the Communist 
Party, they resort to Islamic extremism. On the nat ional and international arena, they 
always pose to be the saviours of Islam. But if even a word is spoken about Communist 
Party, then Islamic extremism and mine: ity extremism come in. This is happening here 
also, and that is why, I wished to respond to comrade Yechury's remarks. We did not expect

are treated badly anywhere in India the Communists have been the first to react, be it 
Gujarat or anywhere else. But when it came in West Bengal, the words Shri Yechury used

extremism'. But whenever anything happens anywhere in the world in Muslim-dominated

because when Mr. Madani expressed his views, he expressed mine too. 
Coming back to Nandigram, I had a chance to go to Nandigram after the March incident. 
I would not repeat the things said by Sushmaji and others here; the situation there is 
pathetic. Whatever happens, whether it is laying of road or displacement due to anything else, 
90 per cent of the affected people are Muslims. Nobody is talking about that, everybody is 
talking about farmers and others. Of course, Nandigram is a beautiful place. We could go 
there only on the scooter; the first thing we saw was a beautiful pond and fertile land. It is 
definitely not fit to be made a chemical hub; that is for sure. In Kerala, we adore Shri 
Buddhadeb Bhattacharya, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, as he is a progressive Chief 
Minister. He readily agreed to scrapping this deal but still this problem is going on. We, in 
Kerala, feel that it is not because of SEZs; it is only because of the fact that the nazist 
Communist Party took a decision that if somebody goes against their party, then they 
would take it personally. The Police is not there; their cadres are coming out. This has 
become a prestige issue for them. Otherwise, Nandigram is represented by the CPI; it is not a 
CPM hold. Still, CPM is taking their cadres, without taking Police protection; it is taking it as

Kerala too, in Kannur; Kannur is also a CPM belt. So, we in Kerala fear that this Nandigram

condemn this sort of attitude towards people, especially the majority Muslims. Thank 
you, Sir, for giving me this opportunity.

SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: Mr. Deputy Chairman, Si r, of the little time 
that is given to me, I want to use half-a-minute for the guillotine that has been applied 
to 'Others' speakers in this House. According to my  information, there were 47 
Members in this House who all in the category of' O thers'. The B.J.P, has 48 
Members and I found the B.J.P, using, at least, one-and-a-half hour and to allot only 
28 minutes to the 'Others' speakers, I think, is pa tently unfair. The Party members 
get time to make sher-o-shayari...  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Mr. Joshi, just to tell you, t he time taken by the 
speakers from 'Others' category so far has far exce eded than the time taken by the 
speakers from all the parties on this debate. The allocated time is 28 minutes, but the 
time taken has exceeded all other parties. That is for your information. 
SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: That is your generosity . We should get that 
as matter of right. 
Sir, I have the largest possible experience in this  House of farmers' movements. I 
have been active in the anti-SEZ movements not only  in Maharashtra but also in 
Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Haryana also. I have seen so many farmers being killed, 
so much blood flowing that I have no trears left fo r shedding and I can't get into 
anything like poetry or shayari while speaking about the fanners' agitation. I look at it 
in a very prosaic and logical way. I was hoping to find some solutions to some of the 
problems that I was facing in the debate that has now lasted for six hours. There were 
accusations, there were counter-accusations, and there was even a hilarious claim that 
the NGOs, the RSS and the Muslim fundamentalists ha d come under the banner of 
Maoists for attacking the CPI(M) Government, and th en there was also a defence 
from the Treasury Benches of the Maoists raising ho w great Mao was. I think the 
Congress Party will accept that. But I did not get any reply to the questions that I was 
facing. 
Sir, the questions very briefly are as follows: 
One, why was the Nandigram area of Midnapore Distri ct of all the places chosen 
for this particular SEZ? Because it is a lush green area, a very fertile agriculture area 
and the only advantage that it has is that it is closer to some of the water sources which 
was actually used for throwing away the bodies on 1 4th March and again on 16th 
November. But that could have also been useful for taking away the effluents from the 
chemical industry. But apart from that, there is no reason why that region should have 
been chosen. 
I come from Maharashtra and in Maharashtra we have found out a way. The 
principle that we accepted is that those farmers wh o want to continue doing 
agriculture, their land can't be taken away by anybody, and those farmers who do not 
want to continue with agriculture, they have the fu ll right to dispose of their land to 
anybody they like, at whatever price they like and whenever they like. Once this 
principle is accepted, we were able to formulate bodies where the farmers themselves 
undertook the development of the Special Economic Z ones and therefore there has 
not been any kind of conflagration that we are seeing in Nandigram. 
Then, somebody, mentioned that 90 per cent of the p eople who were dead and 
injured were Muslims. Why has that happened? There should be some kind of an 
explanation for that

What was the great high about the idea 'recapture'? Were the people driven out? Why 
did they go out? What about the high about recapture? 
The last question is: Why is it that the ruling par ty in Bengal is using the kind of 
brazenness that was used after Tiananmen Square operation by the Chinese rulers? 
Normally, the Communists do not do that. They very politely try to understand the 
point of view of the other people and try to find a solution. Why is it that they are going 
it? Mr. A.B. Bardhan, with whom I had a talk he is the General Secretary of the CPI 
said that this was the arrogance of power. I don't know if this is the arrogance of 
power or they are in the flush of the recent victor y in Bengal. But this is something 
that I did not expect from them. 
Sir, I also visited Nandigram twice and I took the occasion to go out and talk to the 
people and farmers who were there. The facts that cannot be denied very briefly are as 
follows: On 14th March, two facts were established. The police forces in West Bengal 
have been largely infiltrated and that there has been a deliberate effort to push the party 
cadres into the police force officially. Secondly, there has been a large degree of 
indoctrination of the police forces which is also o f course understandable as this has 
happened in every communist country. Then on 14th M arch again, it was said that 
eight people were killed in the police firing because the bullets were known to be the 
police bullets and six people were killed by the bullets that did not belong to the police. 
Everybody admitted that many people who were using even private firearms and 
wearing uniforms were actually CPI(M) cadre people. It was established later on in the 
CBI inquiry that they were CPI(M) fellows who carri ed on as police people. On 16th 
November, a different thing happened. Now, they were not the private CPI(M) people 
masquerading as police forces. They were ordinary p eople who were looking like 
farmers. They called themselves 'red army' and in a  very military-like operation 
marched over to Nandigram. They put the hostages of  the anti-acquisition people in 
the front, in between, there were the people, CPI(M ) cadres, who were driven out, 
who were supposed to take over and resettle in the villages and the 'red army' was 
firing from behind both of them. The people in the villages did not reply because they 
not want to kill their own brothers. These are the facts which have been established. 
The number of people killed in the months of March was said to be only 14. In fact, 
from the local enquiries, I found that, at least, 200 people were missing and they were 
presumed to be dead. There are witnesses who say th at the dead bodies were 
carried in truckloads and put into the river. Simil arly, the number of people dead in the 
month November and missing as of today, is 400. Sir , I tried to enquire from the 
farmers what lies behind all this. Sir, the simple story, I will try to explain in the way 
Sherlock Holmes explains at the end of the novel, the mystery of the whole Nandigram 
affair. The brazenness of the ruling party comes from the fact that behind Nandigram lies 
a very serious skeletons in their cupboards and they are very keen to hide them. What 
is the skeleton? The skeleton is this. The Communis t Party and the Left front people 
always brage about their land reform programme. The fact is that the land reforms have 
happened in Midnapore and this is the area where ma ximum land reforms have 
happened. Therefore, the Communist Party thought that this is an area where all the 
people who are land-owners are now are the benefici aries of the land reforms 
programme and there would not be any resistance. But, in fact, in the operation of the 
land reforms programme, something very funny happen ed. There was a share-
cropping kind of land reform, to which Shri Priyara njan Dasmunsi referred to and 
there were also direct transfer of the land to the original landless people. The funny 
thing that happened was that the documents relating  to land records, either the 
possession or for the share-cropping, were not transferred to the poeple who received 
the land rights or who received the land. All the d ocuments are in party office.

SECRETARY-GENERAL: Sir, I have to report to the House the following message 
received from Lok Sabha, signed by the Secretary-General of Lok Sabha:—

Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, I am directed to enclose the All-India Institute 
of Medical Sciences and the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and 
Research (Amendment) Bill. 2007, as passed by Lok S abha at its sitting held 
on the 22nd November. 2007."

up SEZ in Nandigram, West Bengal, and consequent large-scale violence is 
concluded.

The House then adjourned at twelve minutes past 
eight of the clock till eleven of the clock on 
Friday, the 23rd November, 2007.

2    Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
Import of Wheat  
†*121. SHRI MOTILAL VORA : †† 
SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUB LIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the quantity of wheat imported from foreign countries in the year 2006-07; 
(b) the names of States from which complaints have been received that wheat 
imported from foreign countries is not fit for consumption; 
(c) whether Central Government has got these complaints investigated and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) whether it is a fact that the wheat imported from foreign countries has not been 
found fit for human consumption as per the samples tested by Maharashtra Government? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (d) A Stat ement is laid on the Table 
of the House. 
Statement 
(a) In the year 2006-07,60,79,555 tons of wheat was imported into the country on 
private and Government accounts. 
(b) to (d) Complaints have been received from Maharasht ra State that some samples 
drawn and tested from godowns/Fair Price Shops were  not found meeting PFA 
Standards. After receipt of complaints from the Sta te Government, samples were jointly 
drawn from FCI godowns by State Government and FCI Officials. The samples were got 
tested and found to be conforming to PFA Standards.  The Government of Maharashtra 
has been advised to get the existing stock of impor ted wheat in State Government 
godowns and Fair Price Shops examined for quality a nd to ensure that only wheat 
conforming to specified quality standards are issue d through Fair Price Shops. Under the 
Public Distribution System (Control, Order, 2001, b efore the foodgrains are issued from 
FCI godowns, joint sampling is to be done by FCI an d State Government Officials to 
ensure that only good quality foodgrains are issued  for distribution through the Fair Price 
Shops. Further, the Government have also advised al l State Food Secretaries to ensure 
that during transportation and storage all precauti ons are taken to ensure that there is no 
deterioration in the quality of foodgrains till the y are distributed to the ration card 
holders. State Governments have also been advised t hat stocks available with State 
Government Agencies and Fair Price Shops should be regularly inspected to ensure that 
only foodgrains conforming to the quality specifica tions are distributed to ration card 
holders. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: I congratulate the House for an excel lent debate yesterday. Q. No. 121.

SHRI M. VENKAIAH NAIDU: Sir, I would like to know from the hon.-Minister whether 
it is a fact that the Government after specifying c ertain standards have relaxed certain 
specifications for the wheat imported from Australi a and other places because there were 
widespread reports in the media in various parts of the country. 
Two, with regard to Maharashtra, the Human Rights Commission has gone into the issue 
and has said that this supplied material, food, is not fit for human consumption. Many samples 
were drawn and apanchanama was conducted and it was concluded that it was not fit for 
human consumption. What is the action taken; what is the quantum of it; how serious is the 
problem; and what are the steps taken by the hon. Minister in this regard? 

Oral Answers [23 NOV. 2007] to Questions   5 
 
 SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, I have already said that i n Maharashtra the total 
allocation was 13,97,000 tonnes. Complaints came from Bombay-Thane area and there is a 
district called Sindhudurg. Out of written complaints which we got, there are two types of 
complaints. One, a few individuals have collected some information from some shops. They 
claim, 'from some shops.' Whatever material they co llected was not collected from the 
godowns of the Food Corporation of India; that has been collected from other shops. There 
were some statements from shopkeepers also that tha t particular wheat, which had been 
given to them, was not for Public Distribution System; that was for open market. And there 
was a delay because of certain steps which the Stat e Government took for distribution. 
(Interruptions) It is a factual position. But still we have taken each and every item seriously.

†*122. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: †† 
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the attention of Central Government has been drawn towards the 
irregularities in the distribution of ration in West Bengal;

(b) if so, the steps taken to check the same; and 
(c) if no steps have been taken, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. A number of media reports have been received mentioning irregularities 
in the distribution of ration commodities under TPDS in West Bengal. These reports have 
been sent to the State Government for getting inquiries conducted into them, taking necessary 
action and submitting reports on Action taken. Two reports have been received from the 
State Government. The State Government has reported initation of suitable action against 
concerned persons, including some staff of the Department of Food and Supplies, Government 
of West Bengal responsible for the irregularities. 
This issue has been taken up with the State Government for taking all necessary action to 
streamline functioning of TPDS in the State. The St ate Government has assured to take 
required action. 
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: Thank you, Mr. Chairman, Sir . I am happy that from the 
reply of the Government it is clear that the West B engal Government has finally admitted 
that there is irregularity at their end. 
Is it correct that a Central Minister from West Bengal sought the intervention of the hon. 
Agriculture Minister after violent trouble erupted in several districts of West Bengal? 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, in fact, I want to request the hon. Chief Minister of the 
State that we should allot more for that particular State. Similar requests also came from one 
of my colleagues and additional allocation was made for festival purpose. 
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: My second supplementary is this. Has the attention of the 
Government been drawn to the report that All India General Secretary of Fair Price Shop 
Dealers' Federation, who is leading the agitation against the West Bengal Government, has 
claimed patronage to two hon. CMP leaders of this House. They are not present now. Will 
the Government ensure that action is taken against him, notwithstanding the patronage that 
he enjoys? 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, in fact, we have seen some Press reports including what 
the hon. Member has mentioned. We have sent every r eport to the State Government for 
inquiry and we are expecting a final reply from them. We got some replies on some of the 
issues where the Government of West Bengal has accepted that there are certain small mistakes 
and small irregularities, and they are taking corrective action. But the main demand of the 
State Government was that we should allot more for Above Poverty Line category. The 
Government of India has taken the entire responsbility for the AAY and Below Poverty Line 
Category. But, as for the APL category, it depends on the availability of stocks. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Shri Bal Apte. (Interruptions)...  
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: Sir, he has not answered my question. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Mr. Apte, please proceed. 
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: Sir, is it a fact that the Centre has, in fact, given 
supply of wheat and rice, but the West Bengal Government has faled to lift them and, therefore,

there was scarcity and that scarcity has further enhanced because the cadres of the CPM, 
who are actually the dealers, did not distribute them? 
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN: Please authenticate it. (Interruptions).,.  
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: It is there on record that the CPM cadres  are 
distributors. (Interruptions)...  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Please (Interruptions)... Kindly allow the Question Hour to proceed. 
(Interruptions)...  
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: The Government is run by cadres. 
(Interruptions)...  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Will the please allow the Minister to answer the question? 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, whatever complaint was received, we have referred to the 
State Government. The State Government has replied to some of the cases and communicated 
that they would like to take corrective action in regard to these cases. They have not mentioned 
anything regarding 'a' belongs to this cadre and 'b ' belongs to that cadre. This type of 
information is not there with the Government. But the second important question was asked 
about what was the allocation and actually how much was lifted. Sir, I have got the figures, 
for instance, from April, 2007 to September, 2007. The total allocation of rice to West 
Bengal was 6,52,788 tonnes and the offtake was 5,33,377 tonnes. 
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: Not lifted! 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: In the case of rice, yes, there is a gap of 1,20,000 tonnes, 
(Interruptions)...  
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: Therefore, there is scarcity. 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: The total allocation of wheat wa s 4,34,844 tonnes and the 
actual off take was 4,02,000 tonnes. In the case of  rice, there is a gap and we have 
communicated it to the State Government. Now we have stopped that.

Oral Answers [23 NOV. 2007] to Questions    13 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, I have to make one thing ve ry clear. Actually, the 
Government does not give money to the State. The Go vernment makes allocation for 
foodgrains which are subsidised foodgrains. The hon. Member is right that the subsidy come to Rs. 
23,000 to Rs.24,000 crores. There are no two opinions about it. And, as I said already to the 
House, after we got a report about this diversion, a number of actions have been taken and, 
definitely, there is an improvement. Still there are States where the Public Distribution System is 
not effectively implemented, and that is the reasons why meeting were called on the question of 
food security; the Food Ministers' meeting were also called. The hon. Member has suggested that we 
should request the hon. Prime Minister to call a me eting of the Chief Ministers. I have no 
objection to it. It is a very impportant subject. Substantial money has been provided for the sake 
of poor sections of the society. So, in order to ensure effective implementation of the scheme, I 
would request the hon. Prime Minister to call a meeting and discuss and bring it to the notice 
of all the Chief Ministers. 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Sir, our Government is ve ry much committed to 
strengthening the Public Distribution System for both the APL and BPL categories. But, so far as 
our information goes, there is a huge difference between the quantum of foodgrains requisitioned 
by the Government vis-a-vis the allocations made to the States. Now, I could not hear exactly the 
hon. Minister. So far as my information goes, as far as rice is concerned, 2.29 lakh tonnes till April 
was the quantum of allotment. Then, frorn May, it was reduced to 7700 tonnes. As far as wheat is 
concerned, the figure is 2.93 lakh tonnes. Then, in May, 2006, it was reduced to 9102 
tonnes; and, it was further reduced to 59,040 tonnes from June, 2007. So, when it was 2.93 lakh 
tonnes up to April, subsequently, it got reduced. So, my supplementary to the hon. Minister is 
whether we are committed towards strengthening the Public Distribution System. Considering the 
quantum of foodgrains requisitioned by the Government of India vis-a-vis the actual allotment 
during the last six months, how would the Governmen t of India actually fulfill the total 
requirement of the States so that the Public Distribution System is strengthened? 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: As I have already explained to the hon. House regarding actual 
allotment and actual off-take, now, the information has been sought about the APL and the BPL 
categories. As for these categories, we have not changed the quantum, that is, whatever has been 
allotted for a number of years, and we are maintaining that. Of course, the figure mentioned by the 
hon. Member is correct. But I will be happy to give the figures of allocation of rice for APL 
categories and the actual off-take. In the month of April, 2007, the allocation was 7700 tonnes and 
the actual off-take was 5,662 tonnes. In May, 7700 tonnes were allocated and the actual lifting was 
14,753 tonnes. In June, 7700 tonnes were allocated, and the off-take was 6,638 tonnes. In July, 
the allocation was 7700 tonnes and 13,477 tonnes were lifted ...(Interruptions)  
SHRI M. VENKAIAH NAIDU: Sir, we are not supposed to interrupt the hon. Minister. But 
there seems to be something wrong with the figures. He says, "allocation was 7700 tonnes and 
the off-take was 13.477 tonnes." 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: This is the case in respect of two years when because of festivals 
adequate quantity was given. But if you see the allocation and the actual off-take, practically, except 
two years, the off-take was less than the allocation in respect of APL categories. That is the 
factual position. 
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Mr. Chairman, Sir, the State Government itself has admitted that the 
Public Distribution System was not properly handled. I would like to know from the

hon. Minister whether it is a fact that the ration card holders in the districts of Bankura, 
Birbhum, Burdwan, Murshidabad have agitated against the fair price shop owners that they 
were not being properly given the ration items even  though they have showed their ration 
cards in the ration shops. On the one side, you have been saying that sufficient quantity was 
given. On the other, they have not lifted it. The ration shop owners, against whom there is an 
agitation going on in West Bengal, recently, accord ing to the information which we have 
gathered, are smuggling some of the rice and wheat to Bangladesh. These are the reports. 
Now, who is doing it and how is it being done? It i s happening because there is a price 
differential involved. When it goes to Bangladesh, it is double the price here. Therefore, the 
traders are thriving. Sir, I have my own experience. In my State also, we called those people. 
The hon. Minister of State for Railways is there. Without knowing who the owner is, they are 
booking consignments. This is also one of the lacunae. Therefore, I would request the hon. 
Minister to put an end to all this. Now, you supply whatever quantity of ration they require. 
If it is not distributed, how are you going to fix the responsibility on the State Government?

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Blind population in the country 
*124. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India has become home to the world's largest number of blind 
people; 
(b) if so, how many eye donation banks are available in the country, particularly in 
Maharashtra State and how many of them donate eyes every year; 
(c) how many optometrists pass out every year and considering our population, whether 
they are sufficient to fulfil patients requirements; and 
(d) whether Government has set any target to eliminate blindness or control of blindness 
and if so, the details thereof? 
†[ ]Transliteration in Urdu Script.  

22    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Starred Questions  
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBU MANI 
RAMADOSS): (a) As per the World Health Organization estimates, out of total 37 million 
blind persons (Visual Acuity <3/60) in the world, 6.7 million are in India which is one-fifth 
of the total global blind population. 
(b) As per the Eye Bank Association of India, Hyderabad, there are 500 Eye Banks/Eye 
Donation Centres in the country including 148 in Maharashtra. Around 30,000 donated eyes 
are collected annually in the country. 
(c) There are about 6000 Optometrists in India and about 1200 pass out every year. More 
Optometrists are  needed to fulfill patients' requirements for eye care in the country as the 
Ophthalmologists—para medical personnel ratio shoul d be 1:4. 
(d) As per the survey conducted during 2006-07, the prevalence of Blindness in the country 
has come down to 1% as compared to 1.1% during the year 2001-02. 
The National Programme for Control of Blindness (NP CB) is committed to reduce the 
burden of avoidable blindness to 0.3% by the year 2020. 
The following steps have been taken under NPCB to achieve the targets and for effective 
implementation of the programme:— 
1. Setting up of State Blindness Control Societies and District Blindness Control Societies 
in States/UTs. 
2. Providing Eye care facilities to the needy people at Primary, Secondary and Tertiary levels 
through Primary Health Centres, District Hospitals, Medical Colleges and Regional 
Institutes of Ophthalmology. 
3. Strengthening of Eye Banks in Government/Voluntary Sector. 
4. Financial support to NGOs for strengthening their existing infrastructure for Eye care and 
providing recurring grant for Cataract surgery, School Eye Screening and Eye Donation. 
5. Organizing Eye Donation Fortnight from 25th August to 8th September every year to 
promote eye donation. 
6. Screening of School Children for detection of refractive errors and providing free spectacles 
to poor children. 
7. Strengthening of Regional Institutes of Ophthalmology/eye departments of Medical 
Colleges by providing assistance for development of paediatric eye units/low vision units/ 
retina units and training infrastructure. 
8. Imparting training to Ophthalmic Surgeons from Government Hospitals/Medical Colleges 
for quality eye care. 
9. Intensification of IEC activities Jo create awareness about eye care activities.

Contract Farming 
*127. SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the number of cases of contract farming in operation and cases of corporate farming 
in Maharashtra; and 
(b) what are the steps taken to set up a strong system to monitor contracts, so as to avoid 
exploitation of the workers/growers/farmers? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a ) The State 
Government of Maharashtra has informed that no case s of contract farming have been 
registered in the State so far under the provision of Contract Farming introduced with effect 
from 11th July, 2006 by amending the Maharashtra St ate Agricultural Produce Marketing 
(Regulation) Act, 1963. Since corporate farming does not come in the purview of Maharashtra 
State Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1963 and it is not being promoted 
under the contract farming arrangements, no information is being maintained by the State 
Government in this regard. 

26    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Starred Questions  
(b) Under the provisions of Contract Farming in the Maharashtra State Agricultural Produce 
Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1963, various terms and  conditions, which are to be adhered 
while entering into Contract Farming Agreements, are as under: 
1. Contract Farming Sponsor shall register himself with the Market Committee or with the 
prescribed officer, in such manner as prescribed under the Rules. 
2. The Contract Fanning Sponsor shall get the Contract Farming Agreement recorded with the 
officer prescribed in this behalf. The Contract Farming agreement shall be in such form, 
containing such particulars and terms and conditions, as may be prescribed. 
3. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Contract Farming Agreement or the Indian Contract 
Act, 1872 or any other law for the time being in force, no title, or rights in or ownership or 
possession of agricultural land of the Contract Farming Producer shall be transferred, alienated 
or vested in the Contract Farming Sponsor or his successor or his agent. 
4. Dispute arising out of any Contract Farming Agreement may be referred to a settlement authority 
as may be prescribed in this behalf. The settlement authority shall resolve the dispute in a 
summary manner within thirty days, after giving the parties a reasonable opportunity of being 
heard. 
5. The party aggrieved by the decision of the settlement authority may prefer an appeal to the 
Appellate Authority as may be prescribed in this behalf, within thirty days from the date of the 
decision. The appellate Authority shall dispose of the appeal within thirty days, after giving the 
parties a reasonable opportunity of being heard and the decision of the Appellate Authority 
shall be final. 
6. The decision of the settlement authority and the decision of the Appellate Authority in appeal 
shall have force of the decree of a Civil Court and shall be enforceable as such and the decretal 
amount shall be recovered as an arrears of land revenue. 
7. Dispute relating to and arising out of a Contract Farming Agreement shall not be called in 
question in any court of law. 
8. The agricultural produce covered under the Contract Farming Agreement may be sold to the 
Contract Farming Sponsor outside the market yard and in such a case, no market fee shall be 
leviable. 
Under the Maharashtra State Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Rules, 1967, 
provisions regarding registration of Sponsor with the District Deputy Registrar (DDR), Co-
operative Society have been made compulsory, and this registration will be for one year only. 
The original copy of Contract Fanning Agreement will have to be submitted to the DDR, Co-
operative Societies and the Sponsor shall be liable  to pay cost of supervision to the State 
Government. The Sponsor is prohibited from raising any permanent infrastructure or creating any 
lease hold rights or charge on the land of the farmers/producers, recovery of loans and advances 
given to the farmers/producers can be recovered only from the agricultural produce and in no case 
sale of the land will be allowed, the minimum period of agreement shall be for once crop season 
and maximum period shall not be more than 3 years. Along with this a model draft of the 
Agreement to be entered into between the sponsor and farmers/ producers has also been prescribed. 
Thus, through these provisions, a strong system has been set up in the State to monitor the 
contracts so as to avoid exploitation of the workers/ growers/farmers.

Food riots against PDS agents in West Bengal 
*128. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware of food riots against P DS agents that took place in 
certain districts of West Bengal; 
(b) if so, the details of causes; 
(c) whether Government has taken up the issue with the State Government; and 
(d) what steps are being taken to discount such incidents by improving efficacy of PDS? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) and (b) As per reports received from the State Government 
of West Bengal, there have not been any food riots in the State. However, agitation against 
Fair Price Shop (FPS) dealers has taken place in Bi rbhum, Burdwan, Bankura and 
Murshidabad districts in the State. The main reason mentioned by the State Government for 
the agitation against the FPS dealers is improper distribution of wheat to the APL Cardholders 
by the FPS dealers. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The Government has taken up the issue with the State Government. 
Various reports/complaints received about irregularities in functioning of TPDS in the State 
have been sent to State Government for inquiry, app ropriate action and report to the 
Government of India on the action taken. The State Government has assured to take necessary 
action against all those responsible for irregularities in functioning of TPDS and to streamline 
functioning of the TPDS in the State.
